releases.title: A new appearance, deliberate Canvas loading and clearer recovery
changes: Add Breadbin, an optional home-computer-inspired appearance with light and dark palettes. No appearance is selected automatically or saved copy replaced. Shared transcript fades now stay visible during pointer-based question review while protecting keyboard focus, editing and active embedded reviews.

Keep a running Canvas preview on its loaded definition when newer content arrives. Refresh checks for changes; an explicit Load action changes the running preview, with dirty-state and uncertain-response safeguards.
Track unresolved update failures by cause and occurrence. Let users explicitly acknowledge supported historical uncertainty without claiming recovery, clearing current errors or replaying an update.

Interpret omitted Git refs consistently with Foundation's main default while preserving explicit refs, protected-source checks and exact commit verification. Report missing or conflicting source bindings without mislabeling them as local edits.
Apply the existing durable-checkpoint policy when a managed context uses its default Boundary engine, preserving explicit checkpoint opt-outs and unsupported-engine rejection.

notices.title: Refreshing a running preview no longer replaces its definition
notices.detail: A running HTML or Babylon preview can remain on its loaded version while Canvas reports newer saved content. Refresh is a read, not permission to replace the active preview.
notices.action: Use Load when you want the newer definition. Review any unsaved-state warning before replacing the running preview.

releases.title: Keep saved results and recovery from blocking ongoing work
changes: Prevent background test and coordination updates from interrupting another operation while it saves a retained result or file. Failed saves roll back together, and independent background work keeps its existing scheduling.

Recognize an unsupported source file as a confirmed refusal before a test environment was launched, allowing the existing recovery control to release that unused allocation while preserving the original failure evidence.
Clarify agent guidance for current Work permissions and saved-image comparisons so missing metadata or an older refusal is not mistaken for a new execution block.

releases.title: Recover image conversations and cut repeated diagnostic work
changes: Work archive recovery no longer treats encoded image bytes as text. Updated Work components preserve the original images and history while checking the selected input against the model’s actual limit.

Provider diagnostics now record supported inline images by type, size and fingerprint instead of repeating encoded pixels in event logs and downloadable captures. Original attachments, conversation history and model requests are unchanged; older recordings are retained.
Reduce repeated host updates when a conversation saves tool progress without changing its message or generation identity. Every transcript checkpoint is still saved.
Show specific guidance when required context remains too large or a context checkpoint cannot be saved, without replaying conversation work.

releases.title: Load the app faster while conversations are busy
changes: Reduce repeated HTTPS file-read handoffs when loading the web app or PWA, so a busy conversation does not multiply startup download delays across tiny file chunks. File validation, authentication and bounded transfer buffers are preserved.
Correct update-recovery checks to verify that saved input is released exactly once after a confirmed replacement.

releases.title: Reduce repeated work when saving conversations
changes: Save conversation presentation data with one shared encoding instead of encoding it twice, reducing repeated CPU work while preserving exact history and recovery behavior.
Update the PDF dependency used by artifact tools to pypdf 6.21.4.
Correct a provider setup browser check to recognize a newer completed request without confusing it with an unfinished or unrelated request.

releases.title: Keep work moving while updates wait
changes: Pending application updates no longer freeze conversations, new messages or delegation while waiting for idle. Only the actual installation and restart holds new input; saved messages keep their original identities and are released once the updated app is verified.
Reconcile delayed peer-message acceptance from the original worker after a timeout without resending the message. Uncertain outcomes, Stop and changed conversation ownership remain protected.

notices.title: Automatic updates wait without pausing ongoing work
notices.detail: An update that is ready to install now waits for idle instead of automatically asking running work to yield. Busy conversations can keep an update pending. Older pre-restart holds are released only through their saved receipts.
notices.action: Use the existing Restart now control when you choose to interrupt work for an update. Messages already saved for an update do not need to be sent again.

releases.title: Give Digital Rain sidebar selections room to breathe
changes: Digital Rain now leaves space between the sidebar selection stripe and chat or workspace row contents, matching Lightline's navigation padding. Row heights, rename forms, keyboard focus, animated artwork and shared transcript fades keep their existing behavior. No appearance is selected automatically or saved copy replaced.

releases.title: Keep conversations going when a prepared image request changes
changes: Recover once when a saved image or other prepared request content changes before any model request is sent. Amplifier fits the current request again without repeating completed tools, input or earlier work.
Stop, newer input, changed work authority and uncertain provider outcomes still prevent automatic recovery. This repair does not automatically resume conversations that already stopped.

releases.title: Read with Lightline and carry Full-access work through supported workflows
changes: Choose Lightline in Settings > Appearance for a restrained light or dark reading surface. It supports narrow windows, reduced motion, decoration-off and forced colors without replacing saved appearances. Conditional transcript edge fades now use one shared host-owned behavior, including Digital Rain, while preserving native scrollbar gutters and keyboard focus.

When a new chat changes bundles, show Loading model… until that bundle's inherited model is known instead of displaying the previous bundle's default. Explicit model selections remain explicit; model controls remain available while inherited settings load.

Standing-Full conversations, qualified native descendants and trusted system callers can use the existing model waiting-policy control, manage owner-local schedules and future-run recovery, and start authorized independent chats without an attached browser. These actions retain actual attribution and recheck access, Stop, ownership and destination state; uncertain earlier effects are not replayed.

Trusted Full reviewers and native children can inspect current peer results, retained shared artifacts and saved test evidence through the existing read guards. These passive reads do not grant submission, cancellation or acknowledgement authority.

Discover export and sharing steps through their existing actions, and link a saved Work candidate to its accountable executor before commissioning. Focused unattended-work regression coverage checks native/process/peer-review/artifact and Stop boundaries with explicit controlled-transport limits; this does not claim live-provider acceptance.

notices.title: Full-access work can change global model waiting settings
notices.detail: Chats with standing Full access, their native descendants and trusted system callers can now change the host-wide model queue size and waiting timeout through the existing control. Zero means no count or time limit. Access, Stop and execution checks still apply, and spending limits are separate. Installing this release does not change your current settings.
notices.action: Use Ask for work that should not administer these settings. Review model waiting settings in Settings when you want finite queue or timeout values.

notices.title: Full access supports schedules, recovery and independent chat starts
notices.detail: Authorized Full-access work can manage its own schedules and initiate independent chats without a new browser confirmation. Captured access, Stop, task and native-owner checks remain effective. Exact future-run recovery preserves earlier outcomes instead of replaying them; a fresh trusted-system request has its own checked authority. This update does not create schedules, restart stopped work or change live settings by itself.
notices.action: Use Ask for work that should require human review. Inspect saved schedules and handoff receipts when checking future work, and use Stop or pause when you want work to remain stopped.

releases.title: Save ongoing work for updates and resume it afterward
changes: When a validated app update is ready, current work can finish its admitted step, save its ongoing objective, and continue after the restarted app is healthy. Existing tools and child work settle first; only work yielded by that update is continued.

Messages sent while the app prepares to restart are saved and acknowledged, then delivered in order using their original identities. Stop retains saved messages without sending them, and uncertain or already-accepted input is never replayed.

Assignment managers can send a fresh correction to their completed workers without asking you to restart them manually. Earlier results remain completed, and correction objectives retain the existing allowance and used turns.
Preserve native task progress through completion and restart, and avoid charging the first reserved correction turn twice. Later automatic turns still count normally.

notices.title: App updates can save and continue ongoing work
notices.detail: A prepared app update can now ask automatic work to yield after its current admitted step instead of waiting for the whole objective to finish. Eligible work yielded by this update resumes once the restarted app is healthy. Already paused, stopped, completed or exhausted tasks are not started. Unsettled tools, child work, approvals and uncertain operations remain blockers.
notices.action: Use Stop or pause when you want work to remain stopped. Messages marked saved for the update do not need to be sent again. Turn off automatic updates in Settings if you prefer to choose when an app update begins.

releases.title: Let Full-access agents carry delegated work through to completion
changes: Full-access agents and their assigned child sessions can use the existing configuration, feedback, explicit memory and unused-resource cleanup actions without extra human confirmation steps. Ask mode keeps its review and permission requirements.

Delegated work retains its own task and input identity after a parent turn finishes or a newer parent turn begins. Stop, access changes, ownership, workspace boundaries and exact-result checks still govern each effect.
Full access can continue with incomplete Work context assurance without treating missing context as verified. Ask continues to require that assurance, and uncertain effects are not replayed.

Agents can inspect and explicitly recover their own settled configuration operations, including operator-started setup, using retained evidence and existing recovery actions. The original request stays recorded.
Simplify recovery display and reuse canonical action owners while keeping exact retry receipts and source attribution.

notices.title: Existing Full access covers more app actions
notices.detail: Chats already using Full can now change explicit memory, including deleting notes and their retained revisions; configure memory contribution/use; change unused-code cleanup policy and run cleanup; and finish configuration and feedback workflows without a separate human confirmation. Assigned child sessions can act for their owning conversation under the same standing access. Saved chats, working folders and protected or uncertain resources remain outside unused-code cleanup.
notices.action: Use Ask for chats where you want review before these actions. Review each chat’s access setting before continuing delegated work. Stop and access changes still block new effects; this update does not itself resume paused work.

releases.title: Keep managers moving with less repeated work
changes: Managers can record acceptance of a settled worker’s exact contribution without waking that worker for another model turn. The new assignment.task.complete action preserves Stop, used turns, history and unresolved questions or operations; running, queued or delegated work must settle first.

Keep peer updates deliverable while a task’s progress and constraints change, and retain complete input identities as long-lived conversations grow. Replacing or suspending the objective, Stop and existing permission and budget controls still apply.

Allow later checks to proceed when an earlier test environment is confirmed stopped but its files remain retained after an export or removal failure. Existing limits, physical capacity and unresolved operations remain effective.

Inspect exact saved images shared through an authorized peer request without copying files or granting access to the peer’s whole library. Image errors now distinguish timeouts from unavailable content and describe only the affected model request.

Reduce repeated work when reading conversation pages and saved attention receipts. Manager guidance favors maintained checks, reuse of unchanged evidence and completion of ordinary repairs without invented approval cycles.
Restore broad post-release verification and correct a browser cancellation fixture’s rendering and teardown waits.

releases.title: Receive peer updates while a chat is working
changes: Ordinary peer messages and host result notices can now reach a busy chat at its next supported model-request boundary instead of waiting for the whole turn to finish. When the chat is idle, automatic delivery uses normal admission.

The public coordination.send action adds mode: auto and uses it when mode is omitted. Explicit queue still waits for idle, notify never starts execution, and explicit steer remains tied to its original generation.
Automatic delivery retains each input's identity and respects Stop, task, access and budget controls. Accepted, held or uncertain work is not replayed or redirected to a newer generation.

notices.title: Peer messages no longer wait for idle by default
notices.detail: Omitting mode in coordination.send now selects auto. An eligible message may reach a busy recipient at its next supported model-request boundary; acceptance is not proof that the work completed. Host result notices use the same automatic route. On upgrade, eligible already-queued host result notices also become automatic, preserving their IDs and attribution. Authored queue requests and notices with prior submission evidence are not migrated.
notices.action: Set mode: queue explicitly if your integration requires idle-only delivery. Keep notify for nonexecuting notices and steer for generation-bound input. Inspect the original receipt after an uncertain outcome; do not resend it.

releases.title: Keep permission history out of the way without blocking decisions
changes: Open saved capability decisions from the Permissions history button in chat. History appears in the Canvas overview; current decisions and undismissed old requests remain in chat. Reading history does not change permissions or restart work.
Pending Allow and Deny controls remain responsive while permission history is loading. Newer document or Close intent wins, and dirty editors retain their live state.

Stop intent blocks stale permission decisions before they reach the host. If its acknowledgement is lost, this page can check the exact saved Stop receipt without replaying it; unresolved results remain blocked and a fresh decision is required after confirmation.

releases.title: Keep saved controls intact during cold restoration
changes: Cold preparation now restores saved task, budget, provider and mode controls before writing their combined state. Mounted defaults no longer overwrite controls that have not yet been restored.

If restoration fails or is cancelled before its final save, the original control file remains available for recovery. This does not roll back a failed final write or later preparation, change task-limit authority, or resume work automatically.

releases.title: Confirm saved answers and preserve open reviews
changes: Saved question answers now reconcile late acceptance without resending them. Check delivery reads exact evidence for an unconfirmed answer; missing evidence remains visibly unknown, and a timeout cannot overwrite confirmed acceptance.

Pending New chat keeps the current transcript and interactive reviews mounted until navigation is accepted. A rejected transition no longer discards their live state; message input and configuration controls remain fenced while the request is pending.

Scheduled-task admission records which configuration categories changed between destination creation and input admission. This adds diagnostics without weakening Stop, ownership or configuration checks; it does not establish recovery of an earlier failed schedule.

Native compaction now explains when a smaller continuation could not be confirmed. Original history stays preserved, and the guidance distinguishes a completed compaction call from proof that continuation will fit.
Browser regression checks wait for asynchronous reply copying to finish and retain focused question, scheduling and compaction recovery coverage.

releases.title: Let peer messages and status watches continue without fixed quotas
changes: Messages between two chats and pending status watches now default to no count limit. Optional limits are available in Settings > Testing & resources, and explicitly saved choices remain in force.

A lifecycle event reaches every matching status watch registered before it, including watches beyond the first page. Observation and restart load watch receipts in bounded pages while preserving the event time, expiry, Stop and once-only notification behavior.
Changing these limits does not replay rejected requests or uncertain deliveries. Existing task, access and spending controls still apply.

notices.title: Peer-message rates and status-watch counts are optional
notices.detail: The former default ceilings of 32 messages per minute between two chats and 64 pending watches of one chat are removed. A larger set of matching watches can now receive the same lifecycle event. Explicit finite settings, Stop and task controls remain effective.
notices.action: Use Settings > Testing & resources > Advanced execution limits to choose finite message-rate or status-watch limits. Previously rejected requests are not retried automatically.

releases.title: Keep delegated work moving through long-running coordination
changes: Delegated children can keep using tools and making model calls after their parent turn finishes or a newer parent turn starts. Their original task and input identity remain attached; Stop, access changes and task budgets still apply.
Moving a chat to another checkout lets already admitted child work finish and saves its results before releasing the old worker. Late acknowledgments reconcile the original move without repeating it.

Peer inbox counts now default to no count ceiling, with optional limits in Settings > Testing & resources. Queued senders receive fair turns even behind a long queue, and relaxing a saved limit reconsiders waiting replies.

A coordination request can keep reporting beyond 32 replies or outcome notifications. Result views stay bounded, older receipts remain saved, and upgrading can recover waits stopped solely by the retired notification ceiling without replaying uncertain deliveries.

notices.title: Peer inbox counts are now optional limits
notices.detail: Unconfigured peer inboxes no longer stop at fixed per-chat, per-sender or per-assignment counts. Existing task, spending, Stop and access controls still apply. Saved waits stopped solely by the former notification ceiling can resume through the normal admission checks.
notices.action: Use Settings > Testing & resources > Advanced execution limits if you want finite peer inbox counts. Stop a chat or pause its task when you do not want further automatic continuation.

releases.title: Let available resources guide work and recover exhausted helper tasks
changes: New assignments and unconfigured model queues no longer stop at default member or waiting-call counts. You can choose finite limits or unlimited waiting in Settings; spending limits, Stop and assignment allowances still apply.

Test environments, queued checks and retained resource records no longer have default count ceilings. Machine resource admission, ownership, resource conflicts and uncertain-work protection remain enforced.

Assignment managers can inspect an exhausted helper’s saved task and, with existing authorization, revise its turn limit without asking that helper to spend another turn. Used turns, task history and paused or stopped state are preserved; continuing work is a separate action.

notices.title: Unconfigured work counts no longer have fixed ceilings
notices.detail: New or unconfigured assignment, model-waiting and test-resource policies now use no count ceiling. Existing saved finite choices remain in force. This can allow more work to wait or proceed when its other admission checks allow it; changing a limit does not itself restart work.
notices.action: Review assignment limits and Settings > Testing & resources if you want finite count limits. Managers with existing Full access or verified user authorization can revise a member task’s turn cap; Stop and other budgets remain in effect.

releases.title: Reduce repeated work when agents read conversation state
changes: Agents reuse prepared conversation metadata while reading current app state, reducing repeated work as retained questions and coordination history grow. Separate requests still observe fresh state, and complete historical reads remain available.

Contributor guidance and regression checks now distinguish current work from completed history within long-lived conversations, helping catch repeated copying and history scans without discarding saved work.

releases.title: Share complete appearances as ZIP packages
changes: Import and export ordinary ZIP appearance packages with a stylesheet, embedded images or fonts, and portable author and license notices. Existing CSS import and export remain supported.
Import saves an appearance in your library without applying it. Export the selected library entry, or export the committed appearance without including an unsaved editor draft or temporary preview.

Appearance updates retain existing license notices and reject conflicting attribution before saving. Package validation bounds archive paths, sizes and compression, and accepts styling and supported assets rather than executable extensions.

Archive-only test-environment preservation now retains zero-size named pipes as inert metadata without opening or creating them on the host. Ordinary file exports still reject them, and ownership, complete-preservation and cleanup safeguards remain unchanged. This does not automatically recover or remove previously held environments.

releases.title: Let trusted delegated work carry through with fewer interruptions
changes: Saved access choices now follow the source of commissioned and scheduled tasks. Explicit receiving-chat and destination-workspace choices retain their precedence; unavailable or conflicting source records cannot grant inherited Full access.

Full-access managers can read exact peer results and retained result files without becoming request participants or loading the target conversation history. Existing location, file identity and access checks remain in place.

Full-access work can qualify, preview, create and resume supported observations without inventing a new human message. Native child work retains its original admitted authority across preparation; Stop and revoked access prevent stale work from regaining authority.

Under saved Full access, a root agent or trusted system can submit initial feedback with its own selected files or conversation excerpts without a browser or repeated per-file approval. Files retain exact bytes and destination checks; receipts identify the actual caller, and uncertain delivery is never automatically replayed. Later attachment workflows retain their existing review requirements.

New chat keeps composer and configuration controls from changing the previous conversation while navigation is pending. Drafts and attachments remain preserved through failed or superseded navigation.

Client traffic checks now wait for selected work history to settle before measuring idle rendering. This keeps unrelated background discovery out of causal measurements while retaining checks against revision-only updates and excess rendering.
Read saved outputs and images without copying unrelated conversation history. Output attachments still recheck their original message, task location and transfer state before saving.

notices.title: Full access now carries through more delegated work
notices.detail: Existing Full access choices can now authorize inherited commissioned and scheduled work, exact peer-result reads, supported observations, and initial feedback publication with selected files or excerpts. These actions can proceed without a browser or a fresh approval prompt. Explicit narrower access choices, Stop, ownership and exact destination checks remain enforced. Upgrading does not enable Full access where it was not selected or inherited.
notices.action: Review saved app, workspace and chat access choices. Use Ask when needed for work where you want approval checkpoints, especially before publishing feedback or including conversation excerpts.

releases.title: Keep delegated work moving and control unattended access
changes: Command-line users can inspect and save Full access, Ask when needed or inherited access for the app or a task. Explicit --yolo and --access choices apply before unattended work starts; existing defaults and narrower overrides remain unchanged.

Assignment owners can retire a finished, safely stopped member to free a current slot and later readmit the same chat. Its history, prior results and spending remain retained; uncertain work and active resources still prevent retirement.

Managers receive clearer guidance for revising their own plans within the work you delegated. Coordination no longer stops solely because a fixed hop count was reached; Stop, permissions, execution ownership and saved work limits still apply.

Skip queued question, failure and deferral notices superseded by a newer result. Verified human answers can travel through an authorized chat handoff without granting permissions or resuming stopped work.

A fresh owner request can recover a settled detached member after its current stopped state is verified. Full-access configuration recovery and headless permission settlement use the existing host authority; uncertain old work is not replayed.
Saved-task details load complete long objectives before completion, and running checks can be cancelled independently of an unresolved start or submission receipt.
Canvas file capture follows the task’s actual working folder, including its worktree, while workspace Files keeps its workspace scope.
Browser checks honor the prepared Python environment, and native test fixtures retain their actual input identity. These maintenance changes improve validation of installed packages.

notices.title: Explicit command-line access choices are saved
notices.detail: The new access full command saves the app’s Full access preference. --yolo or --access full on a task command saves that task’s preference. Full access allows supported work without recurring approval prompts; more-specific overrides and Stop still apply. Upgrading alone does not enable it.
notices.action: Inspect the effective setting with amplifier-unified access status. Use access ask to change the app default, or the corresponding task scope to change a saved task choice. Review the chosen scope before enabling unattended access.

releases.title: Faster agent steps and lighter live updates
changes: Allow independent app state, action-list and history reads to run together while preserving their existing permission and consistency checks.
Prepare current app context in one bounded request, retaining completed sections when another section is unavailable.
Keep bridge timing observations in diagnostics instead of repeatedly saving and publishing large conversations.
Avoid rebuilding action schemas during dispatch and decoding live client messages more than once; consolidate shared internal helpers and refresh contributor guidance.
New chats now retain the explicit ownership and working-folder facts needed to inspect their isolated test environments after native runtime startup and reopening.

Failed environment exports retain a bounded verification reason for their authenticated owner, without exposing file content or weakening archive checks. Missing older diagnostics remain explicitly unavailable.
These fixes do not automatically repair incomplete historical ownership records or remove previously held environments; their existing evidence and recovery safeguards remain in place.
Maintenance consolidates browser-fixture readiness and shell-example builds, preserving their existing entrypoints and behavior, and updates repository-selection tests for explicit execution folders.

releases.title: Keep retained chat details out of routine background queries
changes: Routine notice and navigation queries no longer repeatedly parse large retained chat details they do not use. Full-detail reads, unread markers and changes to current chat metadata retain their existing behavior.

Add regression checks that grow retained content independently of chat counts, plus checks for mixed metadata/detail reads and stale-state prevention. Align post-release browser and shutdown fixtures with the current application contracts.

releases.title: Bring Digital Rain to landing pages and keep chat controls clear
changes: Digital Rain now extends its artwork to Home, All chats, All workspaces and the Chats tab of a workspace, while keeping search and reading surfaces distinct in light and dark modes.
Assistant message actions sit below the Digital Rain message box instead of inside it, including on narrow screens.
Shutdown releases passive HTTP read waits promptly and reports interrupted reads explicitly, while preserving the separate handling of effectful commands.
Repair native integration-check setup so its current filesystem module does not conflict with the separate installed-skills fixture pin; application dependency policy is unchanged.

releases.title: Keep background notices from slowing down large chat libraries
changes: Prepare unread counts and review notices without scanning unrelated imported chats. This removes a repeated source of delays in chat loading, app actions and streamed updates as saved history grows. Current titles, read markers, hidden chats and review behavior remain unchanged.

Add a regression check that grows the imported-chat catalog independently of the notice list, so a small response cannot hide an expensive full-catalog query. Release workflows also pin their GitHub Actions to reviewed source revisions.

releases.title: Spend less time rebuilding attention updates
changes: Routine browser updates now read the notice records they need instead of rebuilding old resolved questions across saved chats. Current unread counts, active questions, approvals and errors retain their existing behavior, and complete details remain available when opened.

releases.title: Resume saved conversations with less history-processing work
changes: Reduce repeated scans of saved tool work when a conversation starts or resumes. Recovery now prepares its lookup once, preserving complete messages, saved job results, conflict checks and interruption handling without replaying work.

Add focused browser and runtime performance checks that grow saved history while verifying current controls, synchronization and historical detail access. Contributor guidance now requires measured scaling and behavior-preservation evidence for changes to frequent reads, saves and updates.

releases.title: Keep large task histories out of routine chat updates
changes: Opening Work or chat details no longer repeatedly transfers the full saved task change history. Current objectives, corrections, evidence and linked items stay visible, while complete historical details remain available through the existing task-history reads. Task updates, completion controls and reconnection preserve their current behavior.

releases.title: Avoid unnecessary redraws while keeping chats synchronized
changes: Keep the chat screen steady when a server update only advances its synchronization revision and leaves the displayed content unchanged. Command confirmations, navigation, reconnection and current-state observations still receive every update; changed content continues to render normally.

releases.title: Handle peer notices efficiently and diagnose slow startup
changes: Peer notices load the saved messages they need without also loading unrelated execution history, settings and model catalogs. Native history is still checked and reconciled before the notice is saved; a notice does not start the receiving chat.

If saving a peer notice fails before commit, discard its uncommitted message and navigation changes. Retrying a notice that was already saved returns its existing receipt without duplicating it or waking the recipient.
Retain bounded private startup timings to help diagnose slow conversation startup, without recording conversation text or changing provider selection, startup order or cancellation.
Improve failure evidence for conversation activity browser checks and correct test ownership and navigation setup.

releases.title: Spend less time saving unchanged conversation history
changes: Reduce delays around file reads and app actions in long conversations by reusing verified saved execution history when its complete current content is unchanged. Edited history still takes the normal save path, and each reused record is checked against its saved file and index.

Keep failed-save recovery, chat replacement and retirement, corruption detection and existing memory limits intact. This reduces repeated history-processing work without skipping permission checks or discarding saved actions.

releases.title: Reduce tool delays in long-running conversations
changes: Reuse verified message preparation in long conversations instead of repeatedly encoding the same history when an internal item limit is exceeded. Every message is still checked for edits, and the existing memory limit, complete history and failed-save recovery are preserved.

Process small, already-buffered groups of tool-start observations without unnecessary scheduler waits. File reads and app actions can reach their permission checks sooner; command order, approvals, cancellation and bounded fairness remain enforced.
Correct diagram keyboard checks to close the Details overlay before focusing and scrolling the reader; diagram behavior itself is unchanged.

releases.title: Steadier tool responses and clearer Canvas controls
changes: Avoid resaving unchanged resident conversation histories during native metadata refreshes. Changed metadata, parent links and availability still update; complete messages and execution state remain preserved.

Collect already-buffered runtime receipts with one bounded scheduler yield instead of yielding for each line. Receipt order, size limits, permission and cancellation barriers remain enforced; this does not claim that every live delay is resolved.
Persist exact workspace-identity remaps, including affected chats, selected workspace, pins, settings and Canvas references, without requiring unrelated histories to be saved.

Close a Canvas document with its visible, named tab button, or use Close Canvas to return to chat without discarding open documents or viewer edits. Narrow panes keep full-size touch targets; guarded document closing still protects unsaved state.

Clear a chat’s quote notice when its last quote is removed, while preserving relevant feedback with remaining quotes or commentary-only edits. Correct block-copy checks to verify complete literal Canvas-reference Markdown through editing, reload, Undo, sending and fresh clipboard results.

releases.title: Reduce tool waits while chats work in parallel
changes: Group already-received tool results and routine progress updates before saving, reducing repeated work that can hold up file reads and app actions when several chats are active. Results keep their original order and are saved before the next command; permission checks, approvals and cancellation boundaries remain enforced.
Refresh saved-chat metadata without repeatedly processing an unchanged workspace list. Changes to workspaces, availability, counts, read state and selected history still update normally.

releases.title: Speed up chat lists as saved history grows
changes: Prepare current chat metadata once per directory query instead of repeatedly parsing it while scanning saved history. This reduces delays in recent chats and workspace counts, especially for long-running chats with accumulated questions and coordination records.

Keep current titles, status, permissions, read state, workspace boundaries and saved history unchanged. Every query still observes current metadata; no history is deleted and no conversation work is replayed.
Preserve cached upcoming release notes across restarts as the changelog grows, while keeping its size and entry count bounded.

releases.title: Reduce pauses while long conversations save their progress
changes: Reuse unchanged message and work-history preparation during progress updates, reducing repeated processing that can delay navigation, Settings, actions and streamed replies in long-running conversations.
Keep complete history, accounting receipts and private drafts intact. Nested edits are checked on every save; storage integrity checks, failed-save recovery and update behavior remain unchanged.

releases.title: Clearer handoffs and faster history reads
changes: Chats can explicitly request a return notification when queuing work to another chat. Registration and input admission are saved together, and return status distinguishes a saved report, delivery, acknowledgment and available evidence. Existing messages remain one-way unless a return is requested.
Worker returns preserve the commissioned task boundary across ordinary manager progress updates. Explicit Stop, replacement, recipient permissions and execution ownership remain enforced.

History tools copy only the session fields needed to read or search messages, reducing unnecessary work for large conversations while preserving full message content and attribution. Optional bounded timing diagnostics help locate remaining delays; this is not a claim that every source of slow response is resolved.

Quote feedback stays with the chat that created it, survives a late response in the right chat, and clears when that chat sends. Switching chats cannot carry another conversation’s quote notice into the composer.
Update the Settings upload check to verify the current appearance import action, visible success and duplicate suppression.

releases.title: Portable appearances and steadier parallel work
changes: Choose the optional Digital Rain appearance with light, dark and device modes. Its layered code-rain artwork respects reduced motion, background decoration controls and forced colors; your current appearance is not changed automatically.

Save, import, edit, export and delete portable CSS appearances through Settings or the same shared agent actions. Updates preserve saved identities and reject stale edits; library changes do not apply implicitly. Export before deletion to keep a copy.

Appearance editor drafts survive Settings navigation, closing and same-tab reload. Late operation results preserve newer edits, preview confirmation applies the displayed snapshot, and a new page does not resume an old preview.

A bundled appearance-authoring skill supplies portable examples and verification guidance. Skill discovery preserves an existing loader source, visibility policy, token budget and explicit exclusions.
Keep artifact cleanup making progress while conversations continue saving, with clearer records of reclaimed files and deferred cleanup.

Reuse locked Python, Node and browser dependencies between compatible isolated checks while each task installs its own source. Preparation also avoids a boot-cleanup race that could remove temporary installer files.
Deliver commissioned worker reports across ordinary manager progress updates while preserving explicit Stop, replacement and execution-authority checks.

releases.title: Unblock staged updates behind obsolete conversation refresh state
changes: Staged updates can proceed when an unmounted, idle conversation retains an obsolete configuration-refresh marker from an interrupted legacy settings change. The original settings change, recovery hold and conversation history remain preserved; no configuration change or conversation work is replayed.
Active work, mounted runtimes, operation-bound recovery and unavailable observations continue to prevent this cleanup.

releases.title: Clarify update blockers and repair dependency-blocked handoffs
changes: Updates distinguish conversation work, unresolved configuration holds, global activity and unavailable observations instead of labeling every hold as settings being applied. Sanitized diagnostics report the first failing check without changing activation safeguards or resolving held operations.

A chat whose agent marked its task blocked on a dependency can handle a fresh direct queued peer message while its task stays blocked. Permissions, Stop, task revisions and saved budgets still apply; old suppressed or uncertain messages are not replayed.

notices.title: Dependency-blocked chats can receive fresh handoffs
notices.detail: An agent-recorded dependency block no longer prevents one response to a new direct queued peer message. This does not resume the saved objective or answer its dependencies. Human-recorded blocks, Stop and pause remain protected.
notices.action: Use Stop or task pause when you want to prevent further work. No action is needed for ordinary dependency waits; old suppressed messages are not automatically resent.

releases.title: Repair incremental component updates and keep sent messages in view
changes: Component updates no longer reject a compatible, independently selected dependency merely because another component describes it as optional or as a verified member of the same repository. Explicit pins, local sources, conflicting references and final source validation remain protected.

Updates now distinguish application success from component-update failure, replace stale preparation progress with the failure, and explain source constraints without assuming you edited local files or set an override.
Sending a message keeps following its reply when an automatic viewport change clamps the old scroll position. Deliberate scrollback and focus-driven movement still stop following.
Regression maintenance checks real input acknowledgment, completion-time reading position and updater collection ordering without weakening existing safeguards.

releases.title: Cross-workspace conversations and richer Markdown drafts
changes: Existing same-user chats can exchange attributed messages, replies, results and retained artifacts across workspaces. Workspace labels distinguish similarly named chats; recipient permissions, execution ownership, Stop and budget safeguards remain independent.

The input editor supports fenced code and richer GitHub Flavored Markdown, including tables, task lists and strikethrough, while preserving draft and send content. GitHub-specific syntax that cannot be represented richly remains literal source rather than being discarded.
Component updates align sibling modules with the selected repository revision before installation, while preserving intentional pins and local sources and retaining strict final source validation.

Linux certificate setup now provides safer quoted commands, trust verification and cleanup guidance. The instructions distinguish system trust from browser-specific trust; they do not establish that an existing browser certificate warning has been resolved.

notices.title: Chat messaging can cross workspace boundaries
notices.detail: Authorized existing chats on the same user's host can now communicate across registered workspaces. Messages and retained results remain tied to exact participants and workspace identities; this does not transfer permissions, configuration, execution placement or Stop authority.
notices.action: Check the destination chat and workspace when sending task input. Existing same-workspace workflows remain available; cross-workspace messaging does not grant access to unrelated private files.

notices.title: Enter inside a code block does not send
notices.detail: Typing a fenced code block keeps Enter inside the block, inserting a newline with the current indentation.
notices.action: Use Alt+Enter to leave the code block, or the Send button to send your message.

releases.title: More reliable Canvas and saved-work regression checks
changes: Canvas regression checks now close narrow Details before reader input and measure the visible artifact toolbar, while preserving strict editing, navigation, playback, drawing and no-replay assertions.
Saved delegated-work checks wait for their actual history and capture prerequisites, while continuing to reject genuinely superseded reads and verify exact older request and reply content.

Test diagnostics now preserve the original failure when evidence writing or cleanup also fails, and retain lookup evidence for post-release investigation. This is verification maintenance; production history guards, permissions and runtime behavior are unchanged.

releases.title: Preserve unfinished provider settings
changes: Delayed provider loading no longer replaces an unfinished private configuration edit or key with saved settings. Cancelling navigation keeps the existing editor and unsaved-input safeguards.
Settings reload checks now distinguish confirmed provider navigation from a route change that has not reached the host, without saving private credentials in shared state or browser history.

Updated the locked PDF tooling dependency to pypdf 6.21.2 and verified PDF reading, merging, export and encryption in an isolated installed package. Already-installed or separately resolved runtimes retain their own dependency versions.

releases.title: Compact writing controls and clearer source previews
changes: Model, reasoning, provider and bundle settings now start with a compact overview and focused detail pages. Chat access is available from Add; existing save and permission controls remain in place.

Opening Settings from the keyboard dismisses the Add menu without moving focus behind Settings. Closing Settings returns focus to the persistent Add control while retaining the existing unsaved-edit guard.
Quoted drafts adjust their writing height to the space left by surrounding controls, keeping conversation text and the separate Latest control reachable on narrow screens with enlarged text.

Source-chat previews give long titles, Read only status and Close separate space. Explicit dismissal returns to the original control or its surviving message or current thread when that control disappears, without overriding newer navigation or input.
Maintenance keeps history-diagnostic tests aligned with the explicit detail option and registers the new Composer and source-preview regression checks without changing runtime policy.

releases.title: Clearer chat links and side-by-side Canvas details
changes: Inline chat links keep their saved attachment-time title visible when the destination is renamed. Opening a valid link moves keyboard focus to the destination heading without reloading the page or focusing the composer. Archiving or restoring a destination refreshes links already on screen without changing the current chat.
Canvas Details uses a side inspector in wide panes and a bounded sheet in narrow panes, leaving the existing reader and its controls mounted. The narrow Close header stays reachable while scrolling.
Escape closes Canvas Details before leaving focused Canvas, including from the shared header toggle, while native dialogs retain their own Escape handling.

notices.title: Chat-reference API clients: accept originalTitle
notices.detail: Chat-reference descriptors returned by outputs.attachChatReference, outputs.chatReferences and outputs.read now include originalTitle, the host-saved attachment-time label, alongside title, the current destination label when available. Reference identities and navigation arguments are unchanged.
notices.action: Clients enforcing exact result keys should accept originalTitle. Read current descriptors for current metadata; previously retained command receipts are not rewritten. No action is required for ordinary browser use.

releases.title: Clearer saved answers, compact history and reliable cleanup
changes: Questions with answer choices keep the alternative text editor behind a disclosure. Opening or closing it preserves your draft, and a retained draft opens automatically when you return.

Answered and closed questions start compact. Expanded history puts your saved answer and exact review references before the original question and provenance, while keeping existing delivery and review safeguards.

History discovery reads keep coverage and issue counts concise by default. The explicit discovery-detail option also works through the history action aliases, without changing scope or loading agent runtimes.

Fixed automatic artifact cleanup stalling on large saved state. Unreferenced snapshots can be reclaimed in bounded passes while complete reference checks, re-adoption and cancellation protections remain in place.

notices.title: History API clients: opt in to discovery issue samples
notices.detail: Ordinary history query responses now omit discovery.issues. Coverage, issue counts and sample availability remain available. Opted-in issue samples describe global discovery diagnostics, not only the selected page or workspace.
notices.action: If your client reads discovery.issues, pass include_discovery_issues: true to the canonical history query or history.list, history.shared.list and history.shared.view. Treat the field as optional otherwise. No action is required for ordinary browser use.

releases.title: Retire unused component versions with verified caches
changes: Unused component versions can retire when their extra files are only verified Python import caches. Active and rollback versions, shared runtimes, local changes and unknown files remain protected under the existing retention policy.

Retention now binds source and cache checks to the original file inventory through admission and quarantine. Changed files or runtime sharing defer retirement instead of accepting a later inventory as a new baseline.

releases.title: Clearer work, automation and navigation
changes: Automation separates schedule state from the last run’s result, makes page-local attention details easier to scan, and distinguishes the owning workspace from a new task’s execution workspace. Schedule reviews show the start date in the selected timezone.

Shared Work shows each item’s next action and makes check evidence, candidate identity and limits easier to read. Participant reports, independent checks, human acceptance and shipment remain distinct.

Delegate exchanges show the requesting participant when retained evidence identifies it, rather than guessing Main chat for nested work. Long headings and Copy controls have separate space, and the existing Latest control stays outside the transcript.

Back and Forward retain chronological visits and per-visit workspace tabs. The Recent list keeps a bounded set of destinations; private Workspace Settings edits and dirty Canvas content still require the existing guarded navigation decision.
Maintenance corrects bounded history-reconciliation, historical test-timeout and provider-catalog readiness checks without changing runtime authority or provider refresh policy.

releases.title: Recover browsing and move between working folders
changes: Switching an agent’s execution folder no longer fails just because an associated source or destination contains more than 2,000 untracked evidence files. Repository identity, ownership, Stop and execution checks still apply; file-copy and preservation limits are unchanged.

Conversation browsing can recover on a later retry after temporary storage-allocation failures, instead of remaining stuck after space becomes available. Failure diagnostics retain the stage and error type without exposing private paths or messages.

Maintenance strengthens checks for lazy Work disclosures, diagram render readiness, scoped action receipts and runtime dependency provenance without changing navigation, screen-consent permissions or source-verification rules.

releases.title: Clearer guidance for optional skills
changes: Agents now check whether collaboration skills are available before trying to load them, while respecting your selected skill sources. Missing optional skills are distinguished from failures to load an available skill.
Maintenance updates align verification of background-work events, cached Work details and streamed-message attribution with the supported behavior.

releases.title: Finish ecosystem updates with consistent dependency sources
changes: Fix ecosystem updates that stop while resolving worker dependencies when a retained Git source conflicts with another component’s moving reference to the same dependency. The selected source stays consistent through preparation and qualification.
Preserve explicit source choices and dependency compatibility checks. Failed preparation keeps the current runtime active and does not replay conversation work.

releases.title: Smoother voice conversations and clearer background work
changes: Voice conversations delegate work to your configured backend while keeping spoken replies in the conversation. Backend progress and answers appear inside their matching Working / Worked for disclosure, including nested work, without grouping unrelated activity.

Routine history refresh keeps useful content visible without adding a loading row or shifting the page. Voice call transitions, interleaved transcripts and follow-latest scrolling better preserve deliberate scrollback.

Voice controls retain the exact call or connection attempt they act on. Native delegation, late-input reconciliation, usage reporting and bounded provider-startup diagnostics give clearer results without replaying work or exposing private configuration.

Shared Settings actions let agents open Settings and prepare AI connection drafts through the same controls as the browser. The supported-services catalog remains read-only; selecting a draft does not save credentials or bypass permissions.
Bundled app tools return compact action receipts without changing the original arguments used by Work authorization. Saved outcomes, ownership checks and explicit state readback remain available.

notices.title: Direct voice API callers: identify the call to end
notices.detail: POST /api/voice/end now requires a nonempty id or attemptId. This prevents an old request from ending a newer call. Requests without either identity return 400 missing_call_identity; an identity that does not match the active call returns 409 stale_call. This change requires action only from direct API integrations, not users of the bundled browser.
notices.action: Retain the id returned by /api/voice/connect, or the attemptId supplied for that connection attempt, and include it in the /api/voice/end JSON body. If you send both, both must match. Do not retry a stale end request without its identity. Ending a call does not stop background work.

releases.title: Keep delegated work and isolated checks moving
changes: Fix continuation after a delegated worker returns so the current input is checked separately from its displayed conversation ancestry. Stop, settings, budget and task boundaries remain enforced.

Connect and check a configured remote test machine before allowing new checks. Saved progress survives closing Settings, and qualification verifies execution, result download and cleanup. Existing SSH trust and authentication are required; no credentials are copied and no test host is set up automatically.

Review recorded source, workspace and result-archive sizes for saved tests in Settings → Storage. Bounded pages distinguish complete, remote and unavailable records; these are historical file sizes, not current disk usage or space available for cleanup. No saved evidence is deleted.
Keep Work notifications behind committed message state, fixing a send-revision race while preserving readiness updates and attachment protection across adjacent sends and reconnection.

Let agents acknowledge exact reviewed test results without redundant completion notifications, return compact saved-output receipts, and provide clearer task-brief and child-recovery guidance. These refinements do not cancel tests, alter results or expand authority.

Recover held local test CPU and memory through bounded checks of the original stopped or absent owner. Transfer supported source snapshots above 128 MiB in verified parts, and clean up synthetic FIFO test fixtures so future evidence exports remain verifiable. New prepared Python and browser test environments include process-inspection tools required by Storage safety checks; existing environments are unchanged. Uncertain results and retained evidence stay protected; release guidance covers bounded waits and verified generated-asset imports.

releases.title: Quote directly from messages
changes: Removed the extra Choose passage control and source-picker dialog. Select rendered text to quote a passage, or use Reply for the whole message.
Selections that cannot be quoted exactly now explain why without changing your draft.

releases.title: Keep image previews steady while switching images
changes: Keep generated-image previews at a stable height while another image loads or shows an error, so the gallery and conversation do not jump. Image actions stay tied to the loaded image.

releases.title: Keep delayed execution checks from stopping healthy work
changes: Allow tool execution checks to use the existing host transport deadline, so a briefly busy host does not incorrectly stop a chat or worker after 1.5 seconds. Current permissions, Stop, input and execution-owner checks still apply.
Distinguish a timed-out or disconnected execution check from a Work-precondition refusal, and state when the tool was not run. Checks and tool actions are not automatically replayed.

releases.title: Keep Canvas verification aligned with current controls
changes: Maintain automated Canvas checks for the current document tabs and file Details controls, including narrow layouts, exact file paths and downloads.

releases.title: Preserve image restrictions across delegated work
changes: Keep inherited image-generation payment and file-access restrictions when delegated work passes through a child without an image tool or resumes from saved state. Adding an image tool later does not grant permission for paid generation.
Improve background browser checks for appearance, Canvas, inline media and copied text so they follow the current controls and wait for the state they are checking.

releases.title: Keep sent attachments out of your next message
changes: Prevent an accepted message’s attachment from briefly reappearing in the draft and blocking the next send when delivery confirmation arrives before the refreshed conversation. This also covers guidance sent to an active chat and recovery from a lost response.
Make saved-tool-details verification wait for its test data to finish saving before checking older pages, and align the browser workflow check with its existing setup-time allowance.

releases.title: Keep concurrent test-machine registration reliable
changes: Fix intermittent registration failures when several checks access the same test machine while its identity is first saved. Existing ownership and private-file protections remain in place.
Give background browser verification time for dependency setup in addition to its existing scenario budget, so setup does not consume the time reserved for checking the app.

releases.title: Strengthen release checks and preserve release history
changes: Update automated checks for Settings, conversation configuration, Canvas controls and native worker fixtures to match their current supported behavior.
Store the complete authored release history more compactly, preserving every earlier release entry and notice while leaving room for upcoming releases.

releases.title: Keep update status separate from chat errors
changes: Stop showing unrelated conversation-control errors on the Updates page. Real update failures, active-work blockers and restart controls remain visible and unchanged.

releases.title: Quote passages directly and build clearer replies
changes: Select text in a message and add it directly to your reply. Formatted passages that cannot be matched exactly offer an explained source-selection fallback.

Collect several excerpts in compact quote cards, open their original source, and move or remove them while keeping your commentary and attachments. Controls remain reachable in narrow windows and long drafts.
Keep completed selection controls dismissed after scrolling or resizing, and preserve a newer selection when an earlier quote finishes being added.
Extend the supported reply action to accept ordered excerpts while preserving existing single-passage requests and exact saved source references.
Bring release checks up to date with current Canvas, dependency-storage, startup and worker fixture behavior.

releases.title: Keep managers focused and prepare isolated checks more efficiently
changes: Give managers a compact view of assignment members, current tasks and request outcomes, with links to exact details. Reading the brief does not wake idle chats or replace their original instructions.
Let requesters acknowledge an exact reviewed result so the same completion notification does not wake them again. Changed results still receive their own notification.
Send queued checks to another approved test machine when an earlier target has no room, without double-counting an already admitted job or weakening the final capacity check.
Release a stopped test environment’s stale resource reservation only after its exact native owner is confirmed stopped or absent. Uncertain operations keep their evidence and protection.

Reuse verified Python dependencies across compatible isolated checks while installing and checking each task’s current source separately. Unsupported sources keep the existing preparation path, and unused dependency images follow Storage’s cleanup policy.
Keep malformed dependency observations protected during cleanup, and align first-use browser checks with the current Canvas controls.

releases.title: Keep delegated work and saved history clear and reliable
changes: Read delegated requests, replies and follow-ups in chronological order, with clearer sender labels and expandable operation details on desktop and phone.
Keep saved Work details tied to their original turn when reopening older history or loading earlier pages. Exact operation details remain available after inactive history is released from memory.
Keep a newer bundle catalog and its status when overlapping refreshes finish out of order, including when an older refresh fails.
Recognize the current protected file tools when checking patch placement and file access, while keeping execution permissions and stale-runtime checks intact.
Restore explicit tool controls in idle chats while retaining approval, permissions and current-owner checks. Stopped or replaced work cannot reuse a prior control request.
Align discovery, native-runtime, approval and catalog checks with the current app contracts, preserving their existing safety and recovery assertions.

releases.title: Follow shared work and keep clearer failure and test evidence
changes: Review shared workspace commitments, owners, progress, evidence and unresolved cleanup in one Work view. Inspect saved details across desktop and phone clients while preserving your draft, Canvas and Settings edits. Browsing does not start model work.

Keep shared-work requests tied to their exact source and current input before acting. Changed requests, stopped work and uncertain outcomes retain their checks and evidence instead of silently replaying an operation.
Retain the original cause when a manager turn fails, improving support diagnostics without replaying work or replacing a newer result.

Prepared test environments report their actual Python and build commands, artifact paths and source identity. Optional packaging failures can leave source checks usable; terminated helpers do not report successful preparation. New prepared checks preserve source and artifacts as verified archives before cleanup.
Update Canvas browser checks for the current controls and keep rollback, native-boundary and release-artifact checks aligned with their current owners.

releases.title: Review saved work beside questions and prepare the next message
changes: Review exact saved artifact versions beside a question, with shared preview and Canvas controls. Answer drafts and unsaved edits stay protected, and moving interactive previews requires an explicit reset choice.
Save the model, reasoning effort and bundle for a dormant chat’s next message without starting work. Later changes keep the current selection and runtime ownership checks.
See clearer reasons when a model request cannot be admitted, while retaining evidence for uncertain outcomes. Environment cleanup and queued checks keep their current status visible.
Recover the exact generated frontend assets when a successful CI build finds stale committed files, so owners can complete the release handoff without repeating the build.

releases.title: Collect exact quotes and work more clearly with images and Canvas
changes: Collect several exact passages or whole messages in one reply, with your own commentary between them. Reorder or remove a reference while keeping the remaining quotes, text, attachments and saved draft intact. Saved quotations retain their original wording.

Open attached images in a larger preview, use image controls on narrow screens, and drop files onto the current chat. Uploads stay bound to the draft or conversation where they began, including while creating a new chat.

Keep one full preview for each saved artifact version. Use its compact chat card to preview supported content in chat, move it to Canvas or hide the preview; other clients keep their own choices and unsaved edits remain protected.
Reach the full Canvas overview and open-document list, with usable scrolling tabs, compact document controls and preserved reading position, keyboard focus and reduced-motion behavior.
Review the current scope of an old permission request and dismiss an expired card without renewing access or restarting work. Decision controls refresh stale information and preserve existing grants.

Show the model reported by the current startup runtime without overwriting a newer saved selection. Report source-preparation failures as checks that never started while preserving uncertain outcomes for separate recovery.
Expand automatic smoke coverage for Canvas, quotes, artifact presentation, attachments and approval history, and repair the Compact composer and peer-preview checks found after the previous release.

notices.title: Choose where a saved artifact is shown
notices.detail: Saved artifacts now keep one full preview per version in each client. Most open in Canvas with a compact card in chat; generated images retain their inline default. Moving an interactive HTML or 3D preview may need to reset its local interaction state. Unsaved edits still prevent an unsafe move.
notices.action: Use Preview in chat or Open in Canvas on the saved card. If asked, choose Keep current preview to preserve its local state, or Reset preview to move it.

releases.title: Preview source chats and keep the composer compact
changes: Inspect the source of an incoming message from another chat in a read-only preview. Read earlier messages, refresh the snapshot or explicitly open the source chat while preserving your current draft and unsaved-work safeguards.
Group incoming peer messages with clear sender details and formatted content. Copy the original Markdown and keep older pages in order when refreshing or loading more messages.
Keep the chat composer compact until you need more room. Use the model control below the field for model, reasoning and bundle choices, with usable menus and writing controls on narrow screens.
Reorder pinned chats reliably during rapid changes, preserving the saved order, keyboard focus and mobile controls.
Add compact-composer and peer-preview journeys to the automatic smoke checklist, while keeping the existing composer-options coverage and separate installed-package checks.

releases.title: Faster catalogs, reliable reactions and safer configuration views
changes: Reactions respond immediately while keeping confirmed saves, pending changes and uncertain outcomes distinct. Recent confirmed reactions can inform later model requests without starting a turn or replaying work.

Keep credentials, including Team Pulse keys, hidden when inspecting current or older conversation configuration. Editing redacted settings preserves values only for the same module, connection and source; ordinary user data remains readable.
Reduce repeated work when reading chat catalogs with many saved read receipts. Existing unread state, ordering and bounded results are preserved.
Keep mobile app options below the wrapped header so their controls remain reachable at narrow widths and when header content changes.
Update smoke checks for current chat menus, mobile navigation, browser transport and workflow lanes while retaining drawer, keyboard, draft and Canvas checks.

notices.title: Reactions can inform later model requests
notices.detail: Confirmed reactions to recent messages can be included as feedback in subsequent requests to your model provider. A reaction does not start or replay a turn, and requests that were already prepared are unchanged.
notices.action: Use reactions for feedback you want your model provider to receive.

releases.title: Navigate recent work and review upcoming automation
changes: Go back and forward through recent Home, chat and workspace destinations with new navigation controls and a History menu. History stays private to the browser tab and preserves safeguards for drafts, Canvas edits and unsaved settings.

Review upcoming scheduled work and schedules needing attention in a clearer Automation overview. Create or edit schedules in their owning chat with retained private drafts, explicit timezone previews and fresh confirmation before activation; uncertain past runs are not replayed.
Keep Settings closed after a completed navigation and keep Home reachable on wider touch screens.
Keep a delayed mobile navigation drawer request from reopening over a newer destination, so Search and landing-page controls remain usable.

Stop showing a conversation’s unfinished delegated work as running after its own runtime process has exited. Independent and replacement workers keep their state; saved results are preserved and interrupted work is not replayed or marked complete.
Keep cleanup-ownership and native-chat recency smoke checks aligned with configurable limits and bounded history reconciliation.

releases.title: Keep parallel assignments responsive without unnecessary accounting
changes: Avoid recalculating every member’s historical model usage before each new call when an assignment has no call, token or cost limits. This removes a measured source of coordination delays while preserving Stop, membership checks, configured budgets and protection against replaying calls.
Keep the access-and-approvals browser smoke check working when Settings displays an unread-notice badge.

releases.title: Remove optional per-chat quotas and recover verified cleanup failures
changes: Allow task-chat, per-chat environment and pending-test count limits to be turned off. New execution settings default to no count limit for these controls and no queue-wait timeout; saved limits, machine resource checks and independent safety limits remain respected.

Show the effective saved test-runner capacity settings during setup, instead of reporting obsolete environment quotas that no longer control admission. Refresh the observation when those settings change.

Let test-environment cleanup continue after an exactly recorded archive-verification failure before removal. The continuation preserves fresh archive copies without extracting links, checks ownership again and leaves uncertain removal outcomes blocked.
Make the composer voice smoke test explicitly finish its setup fixture, preventing unrelated first-use settings from interrupting the check.

notices.title: New execution settings remove per-chat quotas and automatic queue expiry
notices.detail: New execution settings no longer cap task chats per source, environments per chat or pending tests per chat. Queued checks default to waiting until capacity is available or you stop or cancel them, rather than expiring after one hour. Existing saved limits and timeouts, and settings retained by already accepted checks, are unchanged. Zero means no count limit or wait timeout; machine resource checks, global queue bounds and ownership safeguards still apply.
notices.action: Review Testing & resources execution settings if you want explicit per-chat count limits or a queue-wait timeout.

releases.title: Keep updates moving and let parallel work use available capacity
changes: Keep test-runner update checks independent of ordinary environment-count quotas while retaining CPU, memory, disk and ownership checks. New managed local test setups use measured resource admission instead of fixed running and retained environment counts.

Allow assignment owners to remove the open-helper and concurrent-model-call ceilings. New assignments start without these count ceilings; existing saved limits, spending budgets, unknown outcomes and Stop remain respected.
Keep stopped-turn failure information available through worker preparation so an authorized recovery can identify the correct failed generation.
Preserve unsaved workspace resource and reservation edits when navigating between Home, chats and workspaces, without replaying pending saves.
Update release-notice and update-readiness smoke fixtures for current installed and pending-runner states.

notices.title: New assignments can run more work in parallel
notices.detail: New assignments no longer default to eight open helpers or eight concurrent model calls. Existing assignments keep their saved limits. Set explicit assignment limits if you want to constrain concurrency or spending; blank execution-count fields mean no count ceiling. Test environments still use machine resource checks.
notices.action: Review assignment settings if you want explicit concurrency or spending limits. Existing saved limits are unchanged.

releases.title: Wait safely for busy assignment capacity
changes: Let queued worker calls wait for active calls to finish when older calls have unknown outcomes. Unknown calls keep their reservations, and existing Stop, budget and concurrency limits remain enforced.
Update automated Home, navigation, archive and mobile checks for the current shared landing layouts, including keyboard navigation and usable phone controls.
Keep the complete authored What’s new history available as the release count grows, within the existing size limit.

releases.title: Keep built-in tool updates consistent with their selected sources
changes: Record the selected source of built-in tools during update preparation, so newer filesystem and bash modules can be validated and adopted without conflicting with stale source records. Explicit source choices and integrity checks remain enforced.

releases.title: Keep update checks responsive during runner checks
changes: Keep a requested update check queued while the test runner briefly checks capacity, then recheck safely and show available app or component updates.
Avoid repeatedly polling a capacity-blocked runner merely because chats are idle. Its pending qualification and normal periodic checks are preserved.

releases.title: Keep updates moving while the test runner waits
changes: Allow app and component updates to proceed while an updated test runner waits for capacity or confirmation of its isolated check. The runner retains its original work and evidence; normal app restart and component safety checks still apply.
Keep the newer app release summary and Update Amplifier button available alongside the waiting runner. Preserve component update progress and results when the runner later completes.

releases.title: Reliable Linux setup and conversation settings
changes: Apply conversation settings correctly when the app starts its worker through uv. Missing worker identity now stops the change before it can leave chat input blocked. Previously unresolved changes still require explicit recovery; nothing is replayed automatically.
Find uv in its standard installation location during setup and managed service startup, with Linux-specific guidance for missing prerequisites and clearer recovery errors.
Keep emergency reset usable when the ordinary startup helper is missing or damaged, while still finding uv in its standard location.
Keep the ChatGPT sign-in button readable across supported themes and interaction states.
Show the relevant release summary before, during and after an update, including when a newer release replaces a waiting update.

releases.title: Keep open Work details available as activity arrives
changes: Keep expanded tool, delegate and model details readable as newer activity moves the recent-event window forward, without rereading unchanged fields. Retention stays bounded and tied to the exact saved source.
Catch up on high-impact guidance for earlier releases in What’s new, including Home and workspace layouts, access choices, task creation and managed-component cleanup.
Improve smoke-test coverage for saved detail previews and exact Copy behavior.

releases.title: Clearer tool details and more useful chat names
