changes: See bounded input hints for unfamiliar tools and nested app actions, including readable two-line previews on phones. Image prompts and paths stay out of compact previews while remaining available through explicit saved-detail inspection.
Read long saved tool results with clear retry controls and formatted JSON, while Copy preserves the exact original text.
Give chats useful names after substantive work begins, ignoring short acknowledgments and allowing an early automatic title to improve as the task becomes clear.

releases.title: Useful saved work details and steadier navigation
changes: See useful command, code, action and failure hints in work steps, then expand saved tool and delegate arguments, results and errors. Older and child-session details load in bounded pages; uncertain historical matches remain clearly labeled.
Read unchanged saved model fields while other work appends to the same log, without false content-changed errors.
Keep navigation usable when queued catalog requests disappear while an earlier read is shutting down.

releases.title: Consistent Home, chat and workspace browsing
changes: Use Focus, Brief and Studio layouts across Home, All chats, All workspaces and individual workspaces, with remembered layouts, reading positions and Focus items.
Find Home in the sidebar alongside Browse and Status, and use clearer Home navigation from other pages.
Keep active filters visible, use Pick up again for quiet read chats, and clear status filters without losing your search. Existing chat and workspace actions remain available.

notices.title: Home, chat lists and workspaces share the same browsing layouts
notices.detail: Focus, Brief and Studio are available across Home, All chats, All workspaces and individual workspaces. Layout and reading position are retained when you visit a chat and return. The sidebar offers Home alongside Browse and Status, and navigation again uses Workspaces naming.
notices.action: Choose a layout on the list you are viewing. Use Pick up again for quiet read chats; clearing the status filter keeps your search. Existing workspace Chats, Files and Details and chat actions remain available.

releases.title: Reliable checkout handoff
changes: Allow the turn arranging a checkout handoff to finish its pending model step without waiting on its own settings change, while preserving task limits and unrelated work guards.
Already-stopped or unresolved handoffs retain their recovery state; this update does not replay them automatically.

releases.title: Safer task controls, test machines and storage cleanup
changes: Cancel an exact queued task request or ask active work to stop cooperatively, preserving its receipt and keeping unrelated work running.
Configure task, environment and resource limits, with explicit independent checks allowed to overlap while ordinary checks keep their ordering and cleanup guarantees.
Use approved remote Linux test machines from macOS and Windows, preserving source snapshots, private connection authority and exact cleanup ownership.

Review unused managed components and runner copies in Storage, with automatic cleanup honoring the global preference and retention period while protecting active work, user changes and rollback copies.

notices.title: Storage cleanup can remove unused managed code copies
notices.detail: Automatic cleanup follows the saved global retention and size policy for proven unused components and runner copies. It protects active work, user changes, saved results and required rollback copies. Archiving a chat does not free its storage.
notices.action: Review automatic cleanup and retention in Settings → Privacy & files → Storage. Inspect the cleanup preview before requesting immediate cleanup; deleting saved work still requires its separate review.

releases.title: Clearer update outcomes and worker diagnostics
changes: Keep a verified successful application update visible when a later component update fails, with separate recovery guidance and affected component names.
Preserve specific worker communication and exit failure labels in feedback diagnostics while keeping private runtime details out of reports.

releases.title: Qualified Incus engine updates
changes: Check and update the managed Incus engine separately from the test runner, qualifying a private candidate before selecting it for future tests.
Preserve existing jobs, explicit source pins, custom installations and the verified runner pairing across engine updates.
Recover completed qualification and observe uncertain operations without replaying tests or changing host setup.

releases.title: Qualified updates for managed test runners
changes: Update the managed test runner through the global update preference, qualifying each candidate in an owned offline environment before using it for new work.
Keep existing jobs on their original runner, preserve explicit pins and custom installations, and retain the current runner, a rollback and generations still owned by active work.
Show qualification waits and uncertain outcomes in Updates, with Retry and Skip controls that preserve the exact update identity.

notices.title: Managed test runners follow the automatic update preference
notices.detail: With automatic updates enabled, Amplifier qualifies new managed test runners in an isolated environment before selecting them for new work. Existing jobs keep their original runner. Qualification may wait for test-machine capacity; a confirmed application update can already be complete while runner work is still waiting.
notices.action: Review the separate application and component status in Settings → Updates. Existing chats and checks can continue during a runner capacity wait; use the displayed Retry or Skip control if qualification needs attention. Fixed versions and custom installations remain protected.

releases.title: Unblock updates after interrupted settings changes
changes: Allow a fully idle chat with an older interrupted settings change to stop blocking staged Smart Tool and application updates.
Keep the affected chat blocked pending recovery, preserve its saved settings payload, and continue to defer updates while work is active or its status cannot be verified.

releases.title: Reliable updates for selected components
changes: Preserve selected component branch choices across preparation and later updates while protecting fixed versions, tags, local sources and custom indexes.

Offer Refresh included components to recover older generated pins in a fresh candidate, including verified dependencies of selected components. Existing workers and rollback versions remain unchanged.
Check the difference between Git branches and tags before offering cached or installed component updates, and keep ambiguous or unverifiable sources protected.
Update HTTP, package-management and Markdown parsing dependencies, and remove the compromised emSign certificate root from the application and test-environment trust bundles.

releases.title: Reliable component preparation and Core updates
changes: Prepare downloaded bundles at the exact source revision checked for the update, preventing stale cached sources from replacing the checked runtime during preparation.
Preserve local and pinned source choices during preparation, and reject copied Git checkouts that redirect writes outside the update candidate.
Check and update app-managed Core wheels from their recorded package registry while preserving explicit custom sources and index settings.
Use the newly qualified test-environment runner for new setups while retaining the original runner for existing environments and their cleanup.
Show clearer component-update failure guidance and restore affected preparation checks in post-release verification.

releases.title: Approved test machines and ordered chat checks
changes: Connect approved Linux test machines through saved SSH connections and route supported checks to available capacity. Each check retains its chosen machine and ownership through interruptions and recovery.
Configure how many checks a chat may queue. Checks run in order, with the next waiting until the previous test environment has finished and its cleanup is confirmed.
Manage remote machine limits and per-chat queue limits in Settings, with saved edits protected against lost acknowledgements and competing changes.
Improve browser verification by waiting for confirmed Canvas state and retaining bounded process-cleanup diagnostics.

releases.title: Wait for model capacity and control test resources
changes: Wait for temporary model capacity instead of saving a budget denial. Global queue and waiting-time controls respect cancellation, current limits and uncertain outcomes.
Share test-machine resource limits across cooperating local installations, with verified machine identity and reservations retained until owned cleanup is confirmed.
Adjust queued-test depth, waiting time, resource budgets and execution deadlines globally. Newly accepted work keeps its saved limits through recovery; edits do not change work already accepted.

Recover qualifying Incus creation results from exact recorded operations. Support current local address metadata and bounded shared-project inspection while preserving older controller ownership and uncertain outcomes.

releases.title: Recover coordinated work and manage test capacity
changes: Let an authorized manager take responsibility for an existing chat in the same workspace while preserving its history, draft, Stop and working folder. Adding a chat does not start it.

Recover settled failed workers, including older failures with exact retained terminal evidence, and reconsider outdated budget denials after a fresh authorized request. Safety halts, current limits and completed work remain preserved.
Set global isolated-test capacity without cancelling queued work or interrupting tests already running.
Finish owned cleanup after qualifying legacy export-limit failures, including when guest removal succeeded but later cleanup needs another attempt.

releases.title: Reliable component updates and managed test commands
changes: Accept a checked component update when uv records its exact commit, while preserving the original branch policy so later updates are still discovered. Changed sources and ambiguous references remain rejected.

Run manually launched isolated tests with their selected prepared environment and restricted workload identity, matching queued tests while preserving command limits, ownership checks and uncertain-result handling.

releases.title: Quiet navigation and consistent chat controls
changes: Mark unread chats as read from Browse, Status or Home using the exact notice you saw. Newer responses stay unread, and approval decisions and error review remain separate.
Keep routine background refresh quiet over existing content so Home and sidebar rows stay in place. Initial loading, errors, Retry and explicit Refresh remain available.
Use the same chat controls, detail level and folder-path preferences in Browse and Status, including pinned project rows and drag previews.

releases.title: Prepare coordinated checkouts and explain update failures
changes: Let a manager inspect and prepare separate working checkouts for its directly commissioned idle chats, with current assignment, permission and configuration checks before changes are accepted.
Preserve completed parallel returns and retire obsolete waits so managers can continue coordinating work without replaying completed operations.
Include the affected component and source mismatch in safe update diagnostic receipts when ecosystem validation fails, while continuing to reject a changed dependency.
Restore post-release browser coverage for existing-folder creation, mobile navigation and settled chat shortcut layouts.

releases.title: Browse work by status and recover coordinated chats
changes: Switch the sidebar between Browse and Status independently of Home. New chat and Search remain available in both modes, with the sidebar toggle always in the header.
Read attention, ready and working chats in clearer Brief and Studio layouts while preserving project scope, Focus position, drafts and Canvas.
Keep rapidly returning sidebar queries from treating an intentionally canceled read as a catalog error, while preserving genuine Retry failures.
Connect computer-use approval choices to the current human conversation, preserving guidance and child-chat context.

Resume an assignment after an uncertain Stop only when native ownership proves its workers have settled. A fresh human request can recover a settled failed member without replaying old inputs or resetting limits and usage.
Apply increased assignment allowances to fresh authorized recovery inputs while continuing to enforce conversation and assignment limits.
Remove sent attachments from the composer as soon as delivery is accepted, including resumed browser copies, without consuming failed sends or newer uploads.

releases.title: Move through Focus and keep Home in context
changes: Browse Focus items with Previous, Next and Start again without dismissing work or changing chat status.
Keep your Focus position when visiting a chat or project and returning, including after a reload. Changing the search or project scope starts a new pass, even when it has no results.
Keep Home free of a redundant header label and stale selected-chat highlights. Window titles and chat recovery notices follow the page you are viewing.

releases.title: Clearer access choices and reliable approval guidance
changes: Choose the app-wide access default from Settings → Privacy & files → Access & approvals, even without a chat selected. Existing chat and project overrides remain in effect.
Run routine operations for task-owned test environments through their existing ownership controls without an extra approval prompt.
Clear obsolete approval cards after Stop, restart, workspace changes or expiration without starting or replaying work.
Add guidance when allowing or denying an approval. Overlapping replies deliver that guidance once to the paused conversation, including child conversations.
Steer an active conversation while a file-access change waits to apply, without starting a new turn under the previous access policy.

releases.title: Resume member chats through their manager
changes: A manager can relay your current instruction to resume a stopped member chat in the same assignment. The request must refer to that member’s current Stop and preserves task limits and usage.
Keep later Stops, changed instructions and duplicate resume requests from starting more work. Completed objectives remain completed, and requests with an uncertain outcome are not replayed.
Restore post-release smoke coverage for Home arrival, stopped conversations, queued updates and appearance-preview navigation.

releases.title: Keep waiting app updates current
changes: Keep checking for newer app releases while an update waits for active work. Prepare and validate the newest known release before the ordinary idle restart.
Check for newer releases from Updates without replacing the prepared update. Offline checks keep that update available; failed preparation of a newer release requires an explicit retry.
Force restart confirmation names the exact prepared version and warns when a newer release is available.

releases.title: Resume stopped assignments and improve phone navigation
changes: Reopen a stopped assignment from its commissioning chat after its workers settle. Keep shared tasks, membership, budgets and usage; old queued messages stay stopped and nothing is sent automatically. Separately paused chat tasks and budgets retain their own recovery controls.
Sending to a stopped assignment now explains how to resume it before accepting a message or starting a worker.
Improve the space available for chat titles and touch targets in the phone header.
Restore smoke-test coverage for fresh Home arrivals, settings, saved media and MCP recovery, with bounded cleanup of test processes.

releases.title: A Home for your work
changes: Start at Home with Focus, Brief, or Studio views of work that needs you, unread responses, running chats, and saved conversations. Returning browsers retain their previous surface.
Home remembers your view, filters, project scope, search, pages, and reading position. Appearance chooses initial defaults without replacing your independent view choices.
Reach Home from the first header breadcrumb, including on phones. Projects and On its own clarify navigation while preserving existing workspace folders and chat ownership.
Project actions remain usable while searches load. New chats recheck the selected project before opening a draft, and unavailable pinned projects cannot silently switch destinations.
Preserve chat drafts and saved Canvas content across Home navigation, and release mobile navigation focus correctly when reopening Canvas.
Protect committed Settings drafts before chat-reference navigation can read them.

notices.title: New browser clients arrive at Home
notices.detail: Home adds Focus, Brief and Studio views of your work. New browser clients open Home; returning clients keep their saved destination. Home remembers its view, filters and position without changing chat ownership, drafts or Canvas.
notices.action: Open a chat from Home to continue working. Use Appearance to choose initial view defaults; your later Home and sidebar choices are independent. Home navigation and shared workspace layouts were refined further in 0.20.188 and 0.20.203.

releases.title: Recover configuration changes and open related chats
changes: Inspect an interrupted conversation configuration change and resume it when saved evidence confirms that nothing was written. Recovery preserves the original permissions and does not repeat uncertain or partially completed changes.
Assistant replies can include Open chat cards for existing conversations. Cards use the current chat title and workspace and preserve unsaved-work safeguards when opening the destination.
Repair apply-patch placement for a conversation’s working checkout while preserving its other saved configuration and controls.

Inspect original test-environment removal requests without restarting work. Cleanup retains verified files, preserves uncertain outcomes, and can finish confirmed preparation cleanup without removing the guest again.
Delegated computer-use tools preserve inherited remote desktop restrictions, and approval cards fit more reliably in the conversation layout.

releases.title: Keep idle chats ready for coordinated work
changes: Idle chats stay available for new peer requests after their worker is retired to free resources or adopt an update. A fresh request can start a cold worker without requiring a manual Continue message.
Explicit Stops, failed turns, and uncertain operations keep their existing protections. Previously suppressed requests are not replayed.

releases.title: Persistent access choices and more reliable coordinated work
changes: Choose Full access for a chat, a workspace, or the app default in Chat info → Access & approvals. The choice persists until changed; narrower overrides and restoring restrictions remain available. Existing preferences are unchanged.
Coordination replies survive routine updates to the same task objective, and task boards show observed worker activity.

Recover owned test environments after artifact-preservation failures. Cleanup preserves artifacts, distinguishes known failures from uncertain effects, and releases ownership only after the environment is confirmed absent.

The accompanying context-managed component update supports compaction after unambiguous interrupted tool calls without replaying tools or rewriting saved history. Existing active workers adopt component changes when safely replaced.

notices.title: Full access can be saved for a chat, workspace or app default
notices.detail: Access choices persist until changed. A workspace or chat override can differ from the app-wide default; this release does not turn existing choices into Full access.
notices.action: Review the affected chat or workspace in Access & approvals before widening access. The app default is also available in Settings → Privacy & files → Access & approvals from 0.20.186.

releases.title: Restore saved model recordings and improve everyday reliability
changes: Saved model requests and responses are accessible from paged Work details. New captures link to their exact call, while older recordings remain available through Show saved recordings. Open calls refresh when saved recordings arrive, and full downloads retain their source ownership.
Reviewed diagnostic capture notices stay reviewed as healthy recording activity continues. New losses or capture errors still raise an alert.

Stopped test environments can export their recorded artifacts without restarting the environment or copying its entire workspace. The export keeps a separate receipt and leaves removal and retention decisions unchanged.

Active conversations reuse their navigation index during streaming. Browser updates prepare shared shell data once per frame, and background navigation queries reuse a bounded workspace summary until its source changes.
Workspace replacements refresh navigation even when the total number of workspaces stays the same.

releases.title: Keep saved Work details and conversation responses current
changes: Saved Work details now notify a newly connected browser when they become ready, including the interval before sidebar registration completes. This prevents a stale loading view after reconnecting or reloading a chat.
Internal completion checks keep their generated verification text out of the conversation response. Their recorded activity and usage remain available without adding a misleading interrupted reply.

releases.title: Review tool changes and manage scheduled work
changes: Saved interactive tool views can compare changed actions and explicitly adopt an updated document. Other open views keep their unfinished input and saved version.

Automation provides a paged overview of scheduled work and its owning chats. Review and resume future new-task runs after configuration changes while preserving uncertain earlier outcomes and Stop decisions.
Hold Alt+Shift to reveal numbered shortcuts for the first nine displayed chats, then press a number to switch through the existing draft and unsaved-view safeguards.
Diagrams expose fit, zoom and layout controls directly, improve default readability and keep authored source and styling intact.
A failed provider account no longer blocks an explicitly selected healthy account. Unavailable selections remain visible and are never silently replaced with another account.

An optional local status interface lets other tools observe active conversations, tools and plan progress without reading transcripts. Unified and an optional CLI hook share the same redacted, read-only format.

Navigation reuses unchanged, completed sidebar results during unrelated activity. Background history queries also encode their inputs in bounded batches, reducing repeated bookkeeping without changing saved content.
Recent Work details recover correctly when a refresh is superseded or a temporary source error clears, while preserving the receipt that identifies the displayed history.
Returning to the browser keeps explicitly closed connection settings closed while still refreshing available connections.

releases.title: Keep Chat info controls steady while usage loads
changes: Chat info keeps its controls in place while usage arrives or refreshes, so a late response cannot move a control out from under your click. Usage details remain available below the chat controls.
Browser checks now exercise delayed usage and workspace-starter responses, including clicks while usage is arriving.
Feedback corrections use reviewed comments and separately reviewed attachments, preserving the original report and later maintainer edits.

releases.title: Start requested chats directly and keep question cards stable
changes: An explicit request to create and start an independent chat in another existing workspace now runs directly, without another confirmation. Suggestions that have not been authorized still offer a review.
Direct starts preserve one saved chat and initial-message identity through lost responses, retries and reloads. Current selections, drafts and file permissions remain intact.
Fixed duplicate question cards after rerenders and reloads. Browser smoke coverage now checks question cards alongside chat handoffs, as well as direct-start recovery.

notices.title: Explicit chat-start requests run without another confirmation
notices.detail: When you explicitly ask Amplifier to create and start a chat in another existing workspace, it can do so directly. A suggestion that you have not authorized still offers a review. Your current chat, draft and file permissions are preserved.
notices.action: Name the intended workspace and opening task when asking to start work. Ask for a proposal or review instead when you do not want the new chat to start yet.

releases.title: Review and start a chat in another workspace
changes: Ask Amplifier to prepare an independent chat in an existing folder, review its destination and exact opening message, then choose Create and start. Your current chat and draft remain in place until you choose Open chat.

Reviewed chat handoffs preserve one saved creation and message identity across retries. Changed destinations or settings require a fresh review, and interrupted or uncertain work is inspected without automatic replay.

Visible Work timers no longer send redundant view reports to the host. Smoke coverage now includes the complete handoff journey, narrow screens, two independent clients and lost acknowledgements, plus Activity checks with both empty and populated inboxes.

releases.title: Keep conversations concise and make work easier to inspect
changes: Incoming messages from other chats appear as compact expandable exchanges. Exact copying, source attribution and links to the message remain available.
Amplifier can acknowledge a human message with a clearly attributed reaction. Your reactions remain separate and can be changed independently.

Execution metrics have independent step, work-summary and conversation controls, selected-field copy and download, and an optional usage snapshot that refreshes only when requested. Unavailable telemetry stays explicitly unavailable.

Feedback corrections offer a private comparison of the original report, the previous read, the latest GitHub text and your proposed correction before confirmation. Corrections preserve original issue text and maintainer edits; original-text editing remains a GitHub handoff.

Isolated workspace checks can prepare locked Python and browser dependencies and keep durable job receipts through reconnects. Workspace controls verify available Docker or Incus setup and retain cancellation, recovery and cleanup evidence.

Expanded smoke coverage exercises compact peer messages, independent reactions, execution preferences and reviewed feedback. Post-release fixture fixes improve selectors, storage timing and handling of legitimate release notices.

releases.title: Recover conversations and clarify setup
changes: Changing a conversation bundle uses a fresh worker process, preserves saved history and model choices, and restores the previous configuration if the new bundle cannot start. Stopping the conversation prevents a queued configuration change from restarting it.

Media previews wait for conversation configuration to settle and recover automatically from temporary changes. Saved tool views report connection status accurately and receive verified reconnection updates without replaying work.

Bundle startup errors retain useful diagnostic categories. Setup and service status distinguish a responding host from an unverified public address; certificate guidance and expected listener errors are clearer.

Ordinary file searches follow the same read permissions as file reading, including inherited restrictions. Interrupted checkout handoffs retain their recovery state until the new execution folder is durably confirmed.

Computer Use, Context Intelligence and Model Routing join the ordinary default capabilities, preserving explicit opt-outs, source revisions and model choices. Desktop restrictions remain effective through nested and resumed workers; Context Intelligence forwarding requires explicit configuration.
Expanded smoke and integration coverage exercises bundle changes, media recovery, onboarding diagnostics, saved tool views, Stories workflows and capability permissions.

notices.title: Additional capabilities for ordinary conversations
notices.detail: Ordinary conversations now include Computer Use, Context Intelligence and Model Routing unless explicitly disabled. Newly introduced Computer Use is read-only and targets the server computer. External Context Intelligence forwarding remains off until configured. Saved snapshot bundles retain their existing composition.
notices.action: Review or disable capabilities in Settings → Configured bundles. Existing explicit access settings and provider/model choices remain authoritative.

releases.title: Approve and revoke companion connections
changes: Approve compatible companion apps by confirming a matching code in the browser. Each approved device receives separate credentials with access limited to its permitted chat operations.
Manage approved devices at /devices. Revocation blocks queued operations before acceptance while allowing already accepted work to finish.
Companion identities and private client state remain isolated across devices and server restarts. Expanded security and browser checks cover approval, restricted access and revocation.

releases.title: Reduce repeated updates and clarify saved worker permissions
changes: Concurrent conversations avoid rebuilding unrelated browser views for unchanged delivery and working-state details. Directory visibility checks read only the fields they need.
Managed checkout moves verify repository identity again after waiting for running work and after releasing its worker, refusing changed source or destination bindings.
A resumed worker explains when saved file permissions prevent an operation and how a new worker can use a later approval. Existing permissions and saved work remain intact.
Expanded checks cover keyboard navigation and compact Settings layouts, exact file grants, resumed worker permissions, and separately loaded recent work details.

releases.title: Keep reading steady while work details load
changes: Conversation reading positions stay steady as work details load and temporary loading notices disappear.

Expanded integration checks exercise native runtime, browser, CLI, filesystem, reset, and context-intelligence behavior in their required environments. Browser checks also verify that their test processes finish cleanly.

releases.title: Recover test environments and preserve conversation reading
changes: Owned test environments offer Check and recover to verify their current state without repeating an uncertain launch or check. Recovery and cleanup remain available when the original backend can still be verified.

Incus cleanup saves verified workspace and artifact files by default, with an explicit option to save the full environment. Failed or incomplete exports retain the stopped environment and available evidence.
Appearance previews end when leaving their settings, including when a delayed preview response arrives after navigation.
Reading positions in earlier imported history survive chat switches and browser reloads using bounded page restoration.
Live calls keep following the latest response when the surrounding layout shrinks, while intentional scrolling still pauses following.
Unchanged browser layout requests finish without waiting for unrelated shared-state updates.
Additional checks cover environment recovery, saved exports, conversation reading positions, and reliable updates.

releases.title: Keep everyday work responsive and queue isolated checks
changes: Isolated workspace checks can wait for available capacity, retain their results, and report completion without repeating uncertain work. The workspace test panel supports the configured Docker and Incus backends.

Managed checkout moves finish at saved conversation boundaries, preserve the original task authority, and verify both source and destination before handing off work. Agent action discovery and routine control replies stay bounded.

Large chat directories reuse unchanged navigation data, and optional titles and plans no longer activate dormant chats. Observed conversations receive shorter streaming batches while background work keeps its existing batching.

Archiving a chat gives visible confirmation and Undo while preserving drafts, keyboard focus, and newer navigation. Earlier message pages retain reactions, support forking from the selected message, and a visible return to the latest messages.

Canvas and Settings protect unsaved input during reloads and navigation. Delayed tool opens and list reordering preserve newer selections and focus; diagram fit, touch, wheel, and pointer navigation are corrected.

Workspace setup reports completed inspections before allowing retries and keeps validation errors beside the affected fields. Task storage retains recovery receipts across interrupted requests and replaced panels.
Failed Smart Tool updates can be retried or skipped individually. Storage failures have clearer update diagnostics, and installation repair keeps recovery files outside the installed-tools directory.

Changing model defaults preserves an existing provider source. Removing the last source override reuses the qualified profile, and new worker profiles correctly retain named local-wheel dependency overrides.

Expanded smoke coverage records ordinary navigation and settings outcomes, copied-history scale checks, and concurrent-worker behavior. Remaining device and account checks and performance targets are tracked separately.

releases.title: Confirm update restarts and keep sidebar selection clear
changes: Updates can interrupt active work and restart into a qualified staged app after explicit confirmation. Saved history and drafts remain, interrupted work is not replayed, and unresolved checkout handoffs still require inspection.
Checkout handoffs refused before any runtime release no longer leave the chat stuck preparing. Existing uncertain handoffs remain protected until reconciled.
The sidebar highlights a workspace only while browsing that workspace; viewing a chat highlights the chat.
Workspace chat lists refresh quietly without inserting an Updating message that shifts the layout.
Sidebar titles use the space reserved for hidden actions. Hover and keyboard focus reveal the controls; Everything mode and touch layouts keep their existing visible actions.

releases.title: Reduce work when reading large chat directories
changes: Agent overviews load large chat directories with less database work while preserving conversation ordering, worker totals, and visibility rules.

releases.title: Keep pinned items available and sidebar refreshes quiet
changes: Pinned chats remain in Recent, workspace chat lists, and search results. Pinned workspaces remain in the workspace list, with their pin controls available.

Sidebar lists keep their existing rows without routine Updating messages during background refreshes. Initial loading and failed-read Retry controls remain visible, and refreshes preserve the reading position.

releases.title: Keep navigation and busy conversations responsive
changes: Consecutive final Work updates now share a save during busy bursts, reducing repeated persistence while preserving event order and control-request handling.
Chat details popovers close when navigating to a different chat or workspace. Inspecting another row without navigating still works.
New task storage stays in the chat working folder and follows current file-access rules. Existing storage remains in place.
Runtime bridge diagnostics retain bounded timing and correlation details to help distinguish worker delays from host handling delays.

releases.title: Keep navigation current while conversations are working
changes: Sidebar activity follows current conversation state while navigation pages refresh. Workspace highlighting follows the current view instead of a remembered workspace route.
Pinned and recent queries can finish while busy conversations update unchanged native recency. Changes to visible titles, membership, availability, or ordering still refresh their results.
Ordinary conversation streaming no longer counts hidden worker history. Work controls and open worker history still receive current counts when needed.

releases.title: Keep open Work details current as responses finish
changes: Open Work steps update when a response finishes or new messages arrive, including final status and usage. Equivalent resident refreshes preserve explicitly opened pages and full-result reads.
Work receipts still reject replaced sessions, changed group ownership, and mismatched step identities.

releases.title: Keep earlier Work steps and saved message reactions available
changes: Current Work groups offer earlier step pages while keeping the initial view bounded. Steps explicitly opened in one browser remain available through live updates without resetting another browser’s view.
Saved message reactions appear on recent and older pages without loading the whole conversation. Imported runtime observations remain read-only.
Workspace details include the merged test environment controls, with retained request identities for checking outcomes and separate controls for storage resources.

releases.title: Show ready chat pages and preserve sidebar reading position
changes: Ready recent conversation pages now appear without waiting for full runtime history hydration. Model, bundle, and compact chat controls use the same display readiness, and failed reads keep Retry available.

Selecting a chat or workspace preserves the loaded sidebar rows and reading position while fresh results arrive. Loading older chats retains the current query identity and no longer reports a false changed-during-read error.
Saved peer-message attribution is restored when a complete bounded page proves its identity. Partial or native history pages remain neutral rather than claiming unverified attribution.

releases.title: Open recent conversation pages without rebuilding archived history
changes: Opening a chat reads a bounded recent message page and root activity window. Older pages load on request; viewing a chat does not reconstruct its full transcript or child-worker histories.
Saved message IDs remain intact. Imported runtime history is a separate read-only view, and partial work pages do not claim complete conversation totals.
Conversation navigation uses already loaded messages and local previews instead of fetching the full history index on every chat switch.
Recovery notices no longer appear inline in the conversation; the original saved recovery records are retained.
Saved history pages can expire when their source changes. Return to the latest messages to start a fresh reading window.

releases.title: Reduce history cache waste and settle navigation updates correctly
changes: History readers reject obsolete event checkpoints before allocating their full contents. Canonical history remains authoritative and the existing memory limits remain enforced.
Pin reordering keeps its pending display until the saved order arrives, preventing the next keyboard move from using an outdated list. App options stay inside compact viewports.

Work completion diagnostics now identify the accepted chat generation separately from the first visible messages. Very large selected Work histories can still exceed the bounded result limit; this release does not claim that case is resolved.

Focused browser checks follow asynchronous navigation coverage and current Settings controls. Release publishing can reuse a matching verified frontend result when GitHub omits the run’s direct pull-request association.

releases.title: Restore chat lists after background reader startup failures
changes: Linux background readers now check their own resident memory instead of inheriting the server’s historical memory peak. This restores chat and workspace lists and allows new history readers to start after the server has handled larger histories.
The existing hard memory limit remains enforced. Large selected histories that exceed that limit still report a separate failure while their memory use is investigated.
Includes the merged workspace resume review and interrupted-outcome repair from the current main branch.

releases.title: Keep cold navigation responsive and reduce history cache memory
changes: On Linux, cold chat and workspace queries run in a bounded reader process so navigation cannot hold the main request loop. Lists show loading, updating or retry status and discard obsolete results.
History index checkpoints are written incrementally instead of making several complete copies. An optional checkpoint failure preserves the readable conversation and completed Work result.
History diagnostics distinguish setup errors from memory refusals and identify the requested chat when reads finish after a selection change.

Workspace collaboration documentation now reflects the delivered coordination features. Browser checks follow the current navigation, Smart Tools and reasoning-selection flows while continuing to detect unintended runtime starts.

releases.title: Keep navigation lightweight and make workspace coordination clearer
changes: Workspace overview brings shared tasks and claims together. Chats can choose write defaults while the server continues to enforce current permissions and accepted-work ownership.
Opening a saved chat no longer prepares a model runtime just to display its history. Explicit preparation and sending a message retain their existing admission limits.

Routing profile fields remain reachable on desktop and compact layouts. Inspected usage refreshes from compact chat updates without losing budget edits, and installed Smart Tools keep their source and removal controls accessible.
Cancelled connection discovery retains ownership of its subprocesses through cleanup. Empty-host verification also closes its owned processes after completing each journey.
History diagnostics record a bounded processing stage and memory measurements when a background Work read fails, without recording conversation content.

releases.title: Keep chat navigation and selected Work processing bounded
changes: Ordinary chat switches reuse unchanged sidebar pages and workspace totals. Workspace listings narrow indexed candidates before applying their existing visibility rules.

On Linux hosts, requested Work histories are rebuilt in a bounded background process. Selected read models reuse unchanged work and apply supported updates incrementally, with exact reconstruction when source changes require it. Other host operating systems retain the existing reader pending native qualification.
Unavailable Work projections show their status without making the saved conversation unreadable. Oversized unchanged histories are not retried repeatedly.
Background verification removes five duplicate source-browser runs while preserving their coverage, and chat timing checks identify the actual displayed conversation.

releases.title: Keep history reads and workspace updates focused
changes: Restoring a chat or adjusting its layout no longer loads older conversation pages without scrolling intent. Switching chats cancels obsolete history reads while preserving accepted work.
Workspace totals reuse their results across unrelated worker updates and chat-title changes. Real membership, activity, unread and availability changes still update the view.
Conversation history checks now explicitly open the requested saved chat instead of assuming the entire library is loaded.
Background browser checks ignore unrelated processes that existed before each scenario, while uncertain cleanup of new processes still stops verification.

releases.title: Make release verification failures easier to diagnose
changes: Background browser verification records each scenario and continues independent checks after a safely cleaned failure, while incomplete or unsafe checks remain explicit failures.
Desktop setup, message recovery, and read-only Work checks now use current fixtures without weakening their original assertions.
The working-set architecture plan now distinguishes delivered improvements through 0.20.149 from the remaining catalog and selected-history work.

releases.title: Keep unchanged chat navigation stable
changes: Native history refresh and the live chat owner no longer overwrite each other’s metadata, avoiding repeated navigation rebuilds for unchanged chats.
Real title and availability changes still update, while active chats retain their stable navigation activity and parent links.
Publishing and selected-view qualification now follow the current Canvas and bounded history contracts.

releases.title: Skip media lookups in chats without linked media
changes: Chats with no linked media no longer request empty media descriptions for each visible assistant message. The server checks the selected chat’s media registry without loading other history.
Linked images and videos still use the existing metadata and file authorization checks. Imported and forked media remain discoverable, including before their first media revision.
Retained-history browser qualification now discovers saved chats through the canonical directory before testing their message windows.

releases.title: Discover interface updates through the live connection
changes: Connected windows receive installed interface identity from the server instead of checking build.json every minute or on focus. Your configured release-check interval is unchanged.
If startup or reconnection fails, bounded version checks can still offer a reload. Reload continues to wait for drafts and Canvas changes to be saved.
Recovery alerts remain readable with saved appearances, and isolated runtime qualification fixtures include the current package boundaries.

releases.title: Keep chat updates focused on the current view
changes: Selected browser views no longer calculate an unused count of every saved chat during routine updates. Explicit listings retain their catalog totals.
Browser acceptance fixtures now follow the streamed navigation contract and locate restored chats through the history catalog.

releases.title: Avoid unchanged navigation refreshes
changes: Empty history-folder bookkeeping and repeated removal of already-absent sessions no longer invalidate chat-list pages. Actual chat and workspace changes continue to refresh their affected lists.
History retention reuses size accounting for the same index within one read, avoiding repeated traversal after cache eviction.

Bounded diagnostics distinguish received navigation updates from changed resources and identify catalog invalidation reasons without conversation content. Selected work-history loading remains under investigation.

releases.title: Stream only the navigation sections you need
changes: Navigation receives changed sections over the existing browser connection instead of repeatedly fetching the complete shell. Unrelated chat events no longer rebuild unchanged navigation pages.
Opening or closing a navigation surface changes only its requested pages. Late responses and reconnects preserve newer page choices, independent windows, drafts and Canvas input.
Shell diagnostics record bounded request reasons and timings without conversation content. Selected work-history reconstruction remains a separate performance investigation.

releases.title: Build only the selected chat context
changes: Ordinary browser updates no longer rebuild duplicate chat and workspace navigation pages. Those pages load through the navigation service when needed.
Worker history is requested only while its dialog is open. Chat summaries retain indexed worker counts without loading the workers, and opening a worker retains its parent link.
Separate browser windows keep independent page requests, drafts and Canvas input. Unrequested or stale worker pages show loading instead of an empty result.

releases.title: Request only the navigation views you use
changes: The built-in sidebar requests pins, recent chats and workspace shortcuts without also constructing hidden search and workspace chat pages. Search and workspace pages load when opened.
Navigation avoids duplicate chat counts and uses direct lookups for sparse pins and archive records. Read receipts, titles and status changes no longer recount the complete library.
Delayed navigation responses cannot replace a newer page choice. Missing page data stays visibly loading, and unfinished edits remain preserved.
Custom navigation components and explicit full-snapshot queries retain their existing interfaces.

releases.title: Keep observations responsive and deliver retained collaboration results
changes: Shared client observations resolve relevant pins and read receipts directly, and page without first counting the complete chat library.
Opening Search chats while a chat selection is still finishing now keeps your newer navigation choice and unfinished draft.
Native ownership queries avoid a costly query plan on older SQLite versions. Cold work-history loading reuses turn and message indexes instead of repeatedly searching the same records.
Collaboration retains result files, revised replies and watches, with explicit configuration grants and runtime provenance.
Task storage allocation, integration validation and collection, return summaries and diagnostics are now included.

releases.title: Keep chat and worker lookups scoped to the requested records
changes: Fetching a few saved chat summaries now starts with their indexed identities instead of traversing the complete saved library.
Worker history pages use indexed parent relationships. Opening a chat no longer scans unrelated saved chats to find its child sessions.
Native aliases, local changes, renamed or moved worker sessions, hidden records and consistent read snapshots retain their existing ownership rules.

releases.title: Avoid repeated workspace scans in large chat libraries
changes: Navigation resolves workspace, pin and archive membership through direct lookups instead of repeatedly scanning the workspace registry for every saved chat. This addresses severe loading delays on hosts with thousands of registered workspaces.
Unchanged directory revisions and chat counts are reused across ordinary selection and text updates. Changes to saved history, read receipts, pins and deletion state still invalidate those results.
Saved chat bodies remain on demand. List queries decode only their requested page; filtering and counts still operate on the disk directory.

releases.title: Load the chats you use without restoring the whole library
changes: Saved chat metadata stays in an indexed directory on disk. Startup, navigation, search pages and workspace counts no longer restore the complete saved library into application memory.
Opening a chat loads its saved owner on demand. Idle owners can leave the working set while their conversations, pending operations, client selections and cleanup protections remain durable.

Warm background history reconciliation reuses unchanged indexed records and updates changed chats without rebuilding every summary in the project. Initial discovery and recovery of a missing index remain separate background operations.
Quiet recorded-work polling skips repeated traversal of an unchanged selected chat. Changed files and newly published work still invalidate that result.
Agent state pages use directory revision tokens to detect changed chat indices, and interrupted collaboration authority is retired before it is shown after a restart.

releases.title: Avoid duplicate history work when opening chats
changes: Queued background history refreshes reuse a completed read when the saved transcript is unchanged; new appends and replacements still load.
Oversized event indexes stop memory sizing once rejection is proven, and bounded metadata remembers unchanged rejection without retaining conversation content.
Performance diagnostics distinguish which kind of saved source changed before rebuilding work records.
Chat Advanced > Computer access again includes the conversation worker readiness checks. Global device readiness remains in Settings.

releases.title: Keep initial chat reads and background cleanup responsive
changes: Idle chats wait for their initial transcript read before background work reconstruction, avoiding an immediately stale duplicate read. Active workers and explicitly requested work remain observable, and cancelled reads cannot leave reconstruction deferred.

Background cleanup uses a cooperative work budget for its complete safety checks. If those checks cannot finish within the budget, all files are retained and cleanup reports that it was deferred. Large retained reference graphs may therefore defer automatic storage reclamation; this is a background work limit rather than incremental garbage collection.

Performance diagnostics separate transcript loading, activity scanning, event associations, work reconstruction and cleanup root checks without recording conversation content. Post-release composer checks follow the current accessible controls.

releases.title: Keep background history work out of everyday chat navigation
changes: Unchanged catalog updates avoid repeating library merges and interface publications. Cold discovery runs in paced, bounded slices; requested chats retain fresh checks, and missed file notifications retain a bounded recovery path.
Storage cleanup reuses bounded, validated file-reference metadata instead of repeatedly parsing unchanged saved resource bodies. Changed or unavailable files still prevent uncertain deletion.

Refreshing recorded work snapshots only the historical identity, lifecycle and accounting information needed to join new events. Canonical request and response details remain available on demand, and older records without canonical logs remain intact.

releases.title: Faster warm chat opening and update activation
changes: Opening a saved chat prepares only the identity, workspace and model configuration it needs, avoiding copies of retained activity and message history. Explicit fork context is preserved.

Background cleanup verifies old runtime generations without blocking current update activation. Proven unused generations are retired with fresh ownership checks, then deleted outside the activation lock. Interrupted cleanup retains its recovery receipt.
Post-release browser checks now exercise the current original-submission retry and new-chat recovery controls.

releases.title: Reduce historical work during live chat updates
changes: Large requested event histories keep bounded, disposable index checkpoints when released from memory. Returning to a chat or reading a new event can reuse parsed descriptors instead of repeatedly parsing old raw recordings; exact recorded requests and responses remain available on demand.
Routine tool and model updates reuse the chat catalog when navigation and attention are unchanged. New leaf tools reuse existing usage totals instead of recalculating every historical model call.

Recent work pages calculate detailed summaries only for the requested groups. History reconstruction indexes worker membership and completed-call matching instead of repeatedly scanning the entire call list.

Performance diagnostics now include bounded operation timings, lock waits, event-loop delays and history-cache counters. These are available to authenticated clients and copied chat diagnostics without recording message bodies or credentials.

Recent model and tool work stays beside the latest messages when a long chat contains many older delegate reports. Work pages follow transcript position, and older details remain available through paging.
Returned delegate reports no longer borrow an earlier turn’s duration or failure. Reports with unknown timestamps do not display invented elapsed time.

Checkout archive, restore and removal refuse chats using a nested folder or path alias. New-chat creation and filesystem moves are fenced against each other, including cancellation, while unrelated chats remain available.
Chat-switch latency remains under investigation. This release does not claim that every live-server delay is resolved.

releases.title: Recover new-chat model settings without refreshing
changes: New-chat model settings reload after missing results or a reconnect. Delayed and failed reads offer an in-place retry while preserving drafts and explicit choices.
Slow default reads no longer block later edits. Concurrent requests for the same draft settings share one server probe.
Available bundles show a selection prompt instead of a loading placeholder when only the inherited default is unresolved.

Unconfirmed new-chat submissions use an explicit retry of their original identity. Empty-chat suggestions no longer appear above recovery messages, and saved-work replay confirmations remain separate.

Mounted reference file and patch tools reject stale worker edits until a fresh read, helping preserve concurrent changes. This protection does not cover shell commands, external editors or other unwrapped writers.
Commissioned helpers share host-owned assignment admission limits and scoped Stop controls. Independent chats retain their own controls; stopping work does not undo external effects.

releases.title: Keep chat switching independent of navigation refreshes
changes: A delayed navigation refresh no longer holds up subsequent chat selections. Continuous background updates cannot indefinitely extend a completed refresh request.
History loading copies only the inputs needed to read messages and paging anchors, avoiding unrelated execution and configuration payloads.
Long execution histories use indexed message placement and grouped turn timing instead of repeatedly scanning the complete history.
Further investigation of intermittent server latency continues. These fixes do not establish that every live-server delay is resolved.

releases.title: Faster chat navigation and background maintenance
changes: Opening a chat from its workspace immediately shows the chat loading view. Reasoning-effort changes stay selected when background updates arrive during a slider gesture.

Workspace plan summaries read root plan receipts without rebuilding child histories or the full execution view. Changing transcripts get one fresh read attempt, and one failed chat read no longer discards every other chat’s event index.

Background storage cleanup releases the app lock while reading resource bodies and revalidates reachability before deleting anything. Raw model recordings are formatted when opened, preserving access to the exact recorded request and response.
Disabled-budget model admission avoids building an unused historical usage report. Tool-result updates reuse unchanged usage totals; admission receipts and enabled-budget checks remain enforced.
An optional, per-window Appearance setting folds interim replies after a proven final response. Final text, media, exports and message identities stay available.
A newer human message invalidates a schedule-repair authorization at both due time and final admission.
Resource reservations retain authenticated ownership and durable outcomes. Independent repository copies preserve original changes and each chat’s selected execution location.
Workspace awareness exposes bounded active-work summaries and advisory file declarations through shared client/server operations; declarations do not reserve files or grant access.
Post-release checks use their declared runtime dependencies and updated fixtures. Broad verification continues after publication.

releases.title: Faster chat controls and clearer navigation
changes: Provider choices load when needed and reuse account-specific cached results. Reading existing chats avoids unnecessary provider discovery, while worker detail remains available on demand.
Long chats spend less time recalculating historical model usage during live updates. Other causes of intermittent server delays remain under investigation.

Transient model timeouts and connection failures can retry the same unfinished request while its worker remains active, without repeating completed tools. Stop, changed turns and partial responses prevent automatic retries.
Diagnostic publication failures no longer hide bridge request outcomes or leave disconnected requests pending.
Workspace and chat pins share one saved order with keyboard, touch and drag controls; an empty Pinned section stays hidden. Unread dots remain visible in workspace chat lists, search and details.
Delegate details show requests, recorded responses and follow-ups with their owning run and expandable activity.
Delegated workers retain their own app identity and inherited file boundaries. Reported artifacts open only when their recorded location and exact bytes can be verified.
Commissioned task chats save their creation request and return notification before the initial brief runs, with explicit outcomes for interrupted preparation.
Installed web-app chat links preserve the intended destination through recoverable launch failures.
Workspace navigation uses explicit destinations instead of implicit return-to-chat controls. Saved document cards show progress while opening and preserve the selected version.
Automatic model-request recovery does not restore a terminated worker or resume a partially delivered response. Native live runtimes retain their own recovery policy.

releases.title: Responsive controls with multiple chat windows
changes: Live browser updates use a dedicated socket so multiple chat windows cannot occupy every HTTP connection needed for images, settings and actions.
Each window retains its own chat, draft and Canvas selection. Reconnect restores current state without replaying messages or model work.
Background history refreshes keep your reading position steady instead of briefly inserting an empty notice above the conversation.

releases.title: More useful chat diagnostics and smoother message delivery
changes: Ordinary messages can move into the next turn when the run they targeted finishes normally during submission. Messages are no longer labeled corrections.

Copy diagnostics preserves the failed turn, includes correlated internal timeout evidence, version information and bounded request timings, and offers manual copying when the clipboard is unavailable.
Read-only media discovery retries a changing conversation snapshot without relaxing attachment identity checks.
These diagnostics help investigate intermittent stalls; this release does not claim to resolve every stall or automatically replay interrupted model requests.

releases.title: Settings that save as you change them
changes: AI connections shows a loading state until provider discovery completes, preventing a brief first-time setup screen for configured accounts.

Diagnostic capture, recording and stream switches save immediately; capture limits and conversation readiness numbers save when you leave the field. Independent changes preserve unfinished connection details.

Notification preferences, existing connection model choices, registered default bundles and idle conversation modes apply on selection. Coordinated credentials, routing, permission and text editors retain explicit saves.
Image generation preferences live in Advanced. The default uses the first eligible provider by priority and is unavailable when none supports image generation.
The recording preference applies when a supported conversation runtime next prepares; already-running runtimes and earlier requests are unchanged.

releases.title: Larger model recordings, smoother chats and clearer progress
changes: New large model requests and responses can be downloaded separately from the bounded preview, with conversation and delegate identity preserved. Partial recordings are labeled with their limits.
Long chats avoid reparsing stable message content when activity clocks tick or you type. Editing, streaming and chat-specific drafts keep their existing behavior.
Canvas accepts GIFs up to 64 MiB within its frame and pixel limits, with playback controls and downloads of the original file.
An explicitly approved schedule repair can be handed to another chat in the same workspace. Resuming still checks the original approval, exact schedule revision, and current stop state.
Activity status aligns with the composer, scrollbars use subtler tracks, and middle-click closes an individual Canvas tab.
After enough comparable completed turns, live status can show a historical duration range. Sparse history, pending decisions and active delegates keep the elapsed-time display.

releases.title: Chat links, GIF Canvas playback and reliable coordination waits
changes: Browser chat links open the requested conversation in that window, including after sign-in, without changing other windows or sending a message.
Retained inline GIFs can open in Canvas with play/pause controls and original downloads. Saved media survives source-file removal, and unsaved Canvas edits are protected.
Media lookup retries once when the saved conversation index changes during a read, while retaining conversation and attachment identity checks.
Coordination waits allow time for the host response after the requested wait period. Transport failures with empty messages now provide actionable details.

Web, terminal and other authorized clients can read shared paginated conversation activity and attention through discoverable APIs, without loading conversation history. Completed reads release their snapshot capacity.

releases.title: Focused workspace storage and downloadable model recordings
changes: Workspace storage counts registered projects beneath the configured workspace root and app-managed files. Running a chat in a home folder no longer makes unrelated personal files part of the workspace total.
Recorded model requests and responses can be downloaded as JSON from model-call details, including call identity and available redaction and truncation metadata.

releases.title: Storage measurements keep making progress
changes: Storage scans now resume across short background time slices until all reachable files have been measured, instead of stopping at the first partial total.
Opening a category reuses the scan cursor and completed folder measurements. Progress stays visible while totals grow; leaving Storage cancels background work.

releases.title: Tolerate metadata updates while reading saved chats
changes: Reading a saved conversation retries once when only its metadata changes during the read. Concurrent transcript changes still stop editing or resuming rather than accepting inconsistent history.

releases.title: Inline media and timely peer results
changes: Assistant messages can retain and play GIF and MP4 snapshots, with explicit playback controls and saved-content identity preserved across reloads and forks.
Active goals consume qualified peer responses before scheduling another continuation. Pause, stop, task revision and capacity checks still govern delivery.

releases.title: Themes shape the whole workspace
changes: Aurora, Atelier and Graphite now vary panel gaps, interior corners, borders and subtle surface artwork across the main screen. Screen edges stay anchored and narrow layouts remain compact.
Theme changes immediately recalculate panel space. Background artwork can be hidden independently, and custom themes retain their shapes and spacing through save, export and import.

releases.title: Responsive storage and consistent settings help
changes: Storage opens immediately and fills in sizes in the background. Bounded scans retain completed folder measurements across drill-downs; Refresh starts a new snapshot.
Folder names appear before their size calculations finish. Slow or very large locations show partial totals, and leaving Storage stops further scanning.
Settings beside a help chat now receives the same connection scope, operation status and page data as the Settings modal.

releases.title: Automatic public repository access recovery
changes: Repair and in-app downloads retry anonymously when GitHub rejects configured credentials, without changing your saved sign-in or Git settings.
Public terminal releases, update reconciliation and feedback metadata can be read without GitHub sign-in. Explicit anonymous mode remains available.

releases.title: Repair without the GitHub release API
changes: Repair and update checks fall back to the public latest-release link when the GitHub API is rate limited or unavailable, before trying account access.
Repair errors distinguish HTTP rate limits, DNS, timeouts and certificate failures. Exact published commits remain the installation source.

releases.title: Public downloads without GitHub sign-in
changes: Repair and update release checks try public access first, so a restricted signed-in account does not block public release metadata.

The installer and repair command support --anonymous to bypass personal Git credentials and URL rewrites for public downloads. The background service can retain the same policy for updates and bundle preparation.

releases.title: Subtle shape and spacing for each theme
changes: Aurora uses softer corners and a little more breathing room; Atelier uses paper-like edges; Graphite uses crisper borders and slightly tighter spacing.
Composer, message bubbles, output cards and controls now reflect their theme. Exact stock themes update automatically; customized skins are preserved.

releases.title: Clearer delegate activity and recording settings
changes: Delegate calls stay grouped by agent and model when work continues after a message or crosses a detail page.
Diagnostic recording shows the saved value separately from unsaved edits, with a nearby recording-only save action.
Chat controls use the sliders icon and Canvas has one header toggle. Saved turn failures show when they were recorded and explain temporary token-counting service failures.

releases.title: More room for your conversation and your work
changes: A continuous application frame gives conversations more room, with quieter work summaries and direct Activity and Settings shortcuts.
Chat overview opens compactly with progress, outputs and relevant context. Documents open alongside chat in a larger canvas, and each view remembers its own resized width.
Document outputs appear as compact cards with an optional inline preview. Images and interactive outputs retain their previews, and narrow chats keep the single Options menu.

releases.title: Clearer settings ownership and help within reach
changes: Global Settings now reads and saves global defaults independently of the selected chat. Workspace overrides for AI connections, images, model rules, modules and sources are available in Workspace Details.
Workspace and global editors keep separate drafts and connection progress, so switching surfaces cannot save changes to the wrong location.
Help me with settings is now beside the close button in the fixed Settings header, including compact layouts.

releases.title: Clean up interrupted chat startup
changes: If startup is cancelled before a conversation worker is registered, Amplifier now waits for that worker to exit and releases its runtime lease. This prevents that cancellation path from leaving a background process behind.

releases.title: Review session storage and browse without repeated scans
changes: Storage now offers reviewed deletion of all saved sessions for a project, or an individual session and its workers. Project working files, CLI settings, credentials and unrelated sessions are preserved.
A single breadcrumb trail replaces the duplicate Back links, with filter and sort controls together on one row.

Storage measurements stay cached during a visit. Navigating back or cancelling a cleanup review no longer rescans; Refresh, a confirmed deletion, or leaving and returning to Storage refreshes the results.
Large history folders no longer consume the measurement budget for other storage locations. Partial measurements explain scan limits or unreadable data.

releases.title: A simpler composer for narrow chats
changes: Use one Options menu for model and agent bundle choices when the chat is narrow. Attachments, dictation, and send or voice stay together in one row.
Keep additional model controls under Advanced model options. Choices and message drafts survive closing the menu and reloading; wider chats keep their familiar separate controls.

releases.title: Reachable chat controls and accurate failed-turn status
changes: Open model and bundle menus in narrow chats without losing them below the screen. Menus stay within the visible window when resized.
Show failed turns as failed even when a runtime idle event arrived first. Previously saved failures also display accurately without changing conversation history.

releases.title: See and manage storage by content
changes: Start with a visual breakdown of workspace files, session data, the app and runtime, backups, caches and logs, and other application data. Nested locations and shared files are counted once.
Open a category for cleanup guidance and a short list sorted largest first. Search, expand the list, or drill into folders and the locations owned by a managed chat.
Review managed-chat deletion, workspace file cleanup with retained chats, and removal of older private backups. The newest backup, shared CLI configuration and active runtime files stay protected.

releases.title: A quieter Ready for you inbox
changes: Review finished responses separately from other notices, with recent responses first and a short list that expands on demand.
Mark all notices, all finished responses, or an individual item reviewed without opening each chat. Questions and approvals remain unanswered until you act on them.
Keep routine completions out of the app attention badge by default. Turn completion badges back on in Ready for you or Notifications; unread chat markers remain available.

releases.title: Simpler image choices and more flexible setup
changes: Choose Automatic, an eligible image connection, or Off directly on the AI connections page. Provider changes save immediately; Automatic shows which connection would currently be used.
Keep image model and workspace preferences under Advanced preferences. Failed saves retain your choice for retry.
Resize the chat and Settings Canvas freely after assisted setup. The initial split is applied only when the setup chat starts, and your adjustments survive navigation and reload.
Use a clearer compact composer in narrow chat panes, with aligned model and bundle selectors above attachment, dictation, and send controls.
Open Settings as an on-demand Canvas tab from the assistant or setup chat. Close and reopen it like other artifacts; ordinary chats no longer include a permanent Settings entry.

releases.title: Workspace storage, progress, and clearer feedback
changes: Explore storage usage in Privacy & files, drill into folders, and review permanent workspace-file cleanup while retaining and archiving chat history.
Archive, search and restore workspaces without deleting their files. See recorded plan progress and expand each chat’s todo list in the workspace view.
Mark chats unread across connected browsers. Keep warnings about unused historical workspaces quiet until those workspaces are used.
Copy Canvas Markdown as formatted text, open Settings with Cmd/Ctrl-comma, and request file reveal on the named owning host when its desktop is available.
Choose optional execution summaries, timestamps and reference identifiers when exporting a conversation.
Send feedback files to a reviewed public or private repository, with explicit confirmation of the exact files and destination. Add reviewed attachments to existing reports.
Inspect another chat’s schedules without changing the active chat. Choose a fallback voice model and speaking voice, and see the model and voice used for the call.

releases.title: Simpler setup, automatic images, and Settings beside chat
changes: Install with one copy-and-paste command, with quiet progress and an optional verbose log. Existing Amplifier CLI configuration is kept. Public update checks no longer require GitHub CLI.
Open AI connection setup whenever no connections are configured. After connecting, choose an optional assistant-led setup chat with Settings in Canvas, or start your own chat.

Generate images automatically using supported connections in provider priority order. Keep provider/model overrides optional, preserve explicit off choices, and never retry an uncertain image request through another provider.
Keep plan expansion across navigation and reload. See the plan in Chat overview, with optional placement above the composer only while working.
Keep reviewed settings notices readable, distinguish initial preparation from an update, and suppress attention badges for routine automatic update work.
Move conversation-specific settings to Chat and Canvas. Clarify that Save & regenerate continues in place unless you explicitly choose a separate fork.
Answer suggested Q&A options with one click, or type your own answer. Prevent duplicate clicks and retain answers when a save needs retrying.

releases.title: Reuse prepared setups and clarify saved worker history
changes: Reuse the prepared runtime when a bundle registration repeats the built-in source or is overridden by an already-qualified source. Actual source changes still receive qualification.
Show saved worker history as read-only instead of offering an unavailable CLI takeover. Keep its transcript and draft available.

releases.title: Edit and fork chats after steering messages
changes: Use Save & regenerate and fork conversations that include messages sent while Amplifier was working, without a false saved-transcript-changed error. Genuine transcript conflicts still require review.

releases.title: Read PDFs and reveal long workspace names
changes: Open workspace PDFs in Canvas with page navigation, zoom, fit width, and selectable text. Download the saved original file, including when a document cannot be previewed.
Reveal long workspace names and location labels on hover or keyboard focus, without redundant tooltips. Workspace details remain available in the flyout.

releases.title: Dictate drafts and navigate documents more easily
changes: Dictate into your draft with a separate microphone button in supported browsers. Automatic shows it on desktop and hides it on iOS and Android; change this browser’s preference in Settings → Voice.
Search chats with one focus outline and one clear button.
Keep following live voice transcripts after ordinary clicks, while deliberate scrolling still lets you read earlier messages.
Keep the selected Canvas tab visible, show file names on hover, and give downloaded documents useful names.
Open sent Markdown and other text attachments in Canvas while keeping the original download available.

releases.title: Simpler image settings and reliable voice transcripts
changes: Manage image generation in one place under AI connections. Choose a supported connected provider and image model, defaulting to Automatic, and switch accounts in one save.
